**James William Fox** (born **William Fox**; 19 May 1939) is an English actor, known for his work in film and television. He is a member of the [Fox family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_family "Robin Fox family") of actors. Fox's career began in the 1960s through leading roles in films such as _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), _[King Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Rat\_(film) "King Rat (film)")_ (1965), _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ (1965), _[Thoroughly Modern Millie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughly\_Modern\_Millie "Thoroughly Modern Millie")_ (1967), and _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (1970).

In the 1970s, Fox took a break from acting to focus on personal and spiritual matters, returning to acting in the early 1980s. Over time, he built a reputation for playing a variety of roles, including upper-class figures and more serious characters, notably in known for his roles in _[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984), _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games\_(film) "Patriot Games (film)")_ (1992), _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993), _[Jinnah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinnah\_(film) "Jinnah (film)")_ (1998), _[Sherlock Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherlock\_Holmes\_(2009\_film) "Sherlock Holmes (2009 film)")_ (2009), and _[Effie Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effie\_Gray\_(film) "Effie Gray (film)")_ (2014).

Fox won the [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for his performance in _The Servant_, and was nominated for [Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role") for _A Passage to India_. He is also a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards") nominee.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

William Fox was born on 19 May 1939 in London, the second son of [theatrical agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_agent "Theatrical agent")[Robin Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-1) and actress Angela Worthington. His elder brother is actor [Edward Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Fox_(actor) "Edward Fox (actor)") and his younger brother was film producer [Robert Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Fox_(producer) "Robert Fox (producer)"). Fox's maternal grandfather was playwright [Frederick Lonsdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Lonsdale "Frederick Lonsdale").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-foxes-2) He applied successfully to study acting at the [Central School of Speech and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Central_School_of_Speech_and_Drama "Royal Central School of Speech and Drama").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cssd-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career")]

Fox first appeared on film as 11-year-old Toby Miniver in _[The Miniver Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Miniver\_Story "The Miniver Story")_ in 1950.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4) His early screen appearances, both in film and television, were made under his birth name, William Fox.

Fox appeared in the film _[The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Loneliness\_of\_the\_Long\_Distance\_Runner\_(film) "The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner (film)")_ (1962).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) His father, [Robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)"), quarrelled bitterly with [Tony Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Richardson "Tony Richardson") over this, having attempted to forbid his friend from giving his son James (known as "Willie") a part in the film. His father claimed Willie had no talent for acting and should not give up his job in a bank.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-6)

In 1964, Fox won a [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), working alongside [Dirk Bogarde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Bogarde "Dirk Bogarde"), [Sarah Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Miles "Sarah Miles"), and [Wendy Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Craig "Wendy Craig").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-bafta-1964-7) On 16 June 1965, [Ken Annakin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Annakin "Ken Annakin")'s period aviation film _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ was released. In this British [period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_film "Period film")[comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film"), Fox is featured among an international [ensemble cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensemble_cast "Ensemble cast") including [Stuart Whitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Whitman "Stuart Whitman"), Sarah Miles, [Robert Morley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Morley "Robert Morley"), [Terry-Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry-Thomas "Terry-Thomas"), [Red Skelton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Skelton "Red Skelton"), [Benny Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Hill "Benny Hill"), [Jean-Pierre Cassel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Pierre_Cassel "Jean-Pierre Cassel"), [Gert Fröbe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gert_Fr%C3%B6be "Gert Fröbe") and [Alberto Sordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Sordi "Alberto Sordi").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-nytimes_066838-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-variety_1200420712-9) Some of the other films he acted in during this time are _[King Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Rat\_(film) "King Rat (film)")_ (1965),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[The Chase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chase\_(1966\_film) "The Chase (1966 film)")_ (1966),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Thoroughly Modern Millie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughly\_Modern\_Millie "Thoroughly Modern Millie")_ (1967),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Isadora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isadora\_(film) "Isadora (film)")_ (1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (1970).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)

### Spiritual life and break from acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Spiritual life and break from acting")]

After finishing work on _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (released 1970, but shot in 1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) Fox suspended his acting career. The film, which starred Fox and [Mick Jagger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Jagger "Mick Jagger"), was deemed so outrageous that critics at a preview screening walked out, with one film executive's wife reportedly throwing up in the cinema.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)

In a 2008 interview, Fox said: "It was just part of my journey...I think my journey was to spend a while away from acting. And I never lost contact with it – watching movies, reading about it ... so I didn't feel I missed it."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tweed-10)

Fox became an evangelical Christian, working with the [Navigators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Navigators_(organization) "The Navigators (organization)") and devoting himself to the ministry.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cinema-11) During this time, the only film in which Fox appeared was _No Longer Alone_ (1976), the story of Joan Winmill Brown,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12) a suicidal woman who was led to faith in [Jesus Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Christ "Jesus Christ") by [Ruth Bell Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Bell_Graham "Ruth Bell Graham").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12)

### Return to acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Return to acting")]

After an absence from acting of several years, in 1981 Fox appeared on television in the _[Play for Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play\_for\_Today "Play for Today")_ "Country" by [Trevor Griffiths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Griffiths "Trevor Griffiths"), a comedy drama set against the 1945 UK parliamentary elections. On film he starred in [Stephen Poliakoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Poliakoff "Stephen Poliakoff")'s _[Runners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runners\_(film) "Runners (film)")_ (1983),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _[Comrades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comrades\_(1986\_film) "Comrades (1986 film)")_ (1986).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He played [Anthony Blunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Blunt "Anthony Blunt") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") play by [Alan Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Bennett "Alan Bennett"), _[A Question of Attribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Question\_of\_Attribution "A Question of Attribution")_ (1992).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He also portrayed the character of Lord Holmes in _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games "Patriot Games")_ (1992), as well as Colonel Ferguson in _[Farewell to the King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell\_to\_the\_King "Farewell to the King")_ (1989) and the Nazi-sympathising aristocrat Lord Darlington in _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993).

Fox has since appeared in the 2000 film _[Sexy Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexy\_Beast\_(film) "Sexy Beast (film)")_,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) the [2001 adaptation of _The Lost World_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lost_World_(2001_film) "The Lost World (2001 film)") as Prof. Leo [Laurence Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Fox "Laurence Fox") in "Allegory of Love", an episode in the third series of _[Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis\_(TV\_series) "Lewis (TV "W.E.")_, written and directed by [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna_(entertainer) "Madonna (entertainer)").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-w/e-14) In 2013, Fox played a lead role alongside [Natalie Dormer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natalie_Dormer "Natalie Dormer") in the movie _A Long Way from Home_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Fox married Mary Elizabeth Piper in September 1973, with whom he has five children, including [Laurence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Fox "Laurence Fox") and [Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Fox_(actor) "Jack Fox (actor)"). Piper died at their home on 19 April 2020.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-foxes-2)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-telegraph_241195-15)

Through his daughter Lydia, Fox's son-in-law is actor [Richard Ayoade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Ayoade "Richard Ayoade").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-telegraph_20170623-16) His former daughter-in-law is actress [Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper"), who was married to his son Laurence from 2007 to 2016.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-BBC_News-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-itv_20160512-18)

**James William Fox** (born **William Fox**; 19 May 1939) is an English actor, known for his work in film and television. He is a member of the [Fox family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_family "Robin Fox family") of actors. Fox's career began in the 1960s through leading roles in films such as _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), _[King Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Rat\_(film) "King Rat (film)")_ (1965), _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ (1965), _[Thoroughly Modern Millie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughly\_Modern\_Millie "Thoroughly Modern Millie")_ (1967), and _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (1970).

In the 1970s, Fox took a break from acting to focus on personal and spiritual matters, returning to acting in the early 1980s. Over time, he built a reputation for playing a variety of roles, including upper-class figures and more serious characters, notably in known for his roles in _[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984), _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games\_(film) "Patriot Games (film)")_ (1992), _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993), _[Jinnah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinnah\_(film) "Jinnah (film)")_ (1998), _[Sherlock Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherlock\_Holmes\_(2009\_film) "Sherlock Holmes (2009 film)")_ (2009), and _[Effie Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effie\_Gray\_(film) "Effie Gray (film)")_ (2014).

Fox won the [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for his performance in _The Servant_, and was nominated for [Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role") for _A Passage to India_. He is also a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards") nominee.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

William Fox was born on 19 May 1939 in London, the second son of [theatrical agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_agent "Theatrical agent")[Robin Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-1) and actress Angela Worthington. His elder brother is actor [Edward Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Fox_(actor) "Edward Fox (actor)") and his younger brother was film producer [Robert Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Fox_(producer) "Robert Fox (producer)"). Fox's maternal grandfather was playwright [Frederick Lonsdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Lonsdale "Frederick Lonsdale").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-foxes-2) He applied successfully to study acting at the [Central School of Speech and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Central_School_of_Speech_and_Drama "Royal Central School of Speech and Drama").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cssd-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career")]

Fox first appeared on film as 11-year-old Toby Miniver in _[The Miniver Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Miniver\_Story "The Miniver Story")_ in 1950.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4) His early screen appearances, both in film and television, were made under his birth name, William Fox.

Fox appeared in the film _[The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Loneliness\_of\_the\_Long\_Distance\_Runner\_(film) "The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner (film)")_ (1962).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) His father, [Robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)"), quarrelled bitterly with [Tony Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Richardson "Tony Richardson") over this, having attempted to forbid his friend from giving his son James (known as "Willie") a part in the film. His father claimed Willie had no talent for acting and should not give up his job in a bank.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-6)

In 1964, Fox won a [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), working alongside [Dirk Bogarde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Bogarde "Dirk Bogarde"), [Sarah Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Miles "Sarah Miles"), and [Wendy Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Craig "Wendy Craig").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-bafta-1964-7) On 16 June 1965, [Ken Annakin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Annakin "Ken Annakin")'s period aviation film _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ was released. In this British [period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_film "Period film")[comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film"), Fox is featured among an international [ensemble cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensemble_cast "Ensemble cast") including [Stuart Whitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Whitman "Stuart Whitman"), Sarah Miles, [Robert Morley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Morley "Robert Morley"), [Terry-Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry-Thomas "Terry-Thomas"), [Red Skelton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Skelton "Red Skelton"), [Benny Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Hill "Benny Hill"), [Jean-Pierre Cassel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Pierre_Cassel "Jean-Pierre Cassel"), [Gert Fröbe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gert_Fr%C3%B6be "Gert Fröbe") and [Alberto Sordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Sordi "Alberto Sordi").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-nytimes_066838-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-variety_1200420712-9) Some of the other films he acted in during this time are _[King Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Rat\_(film) "King Rat (film)")_ (1965),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[The Chase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chase\_(1966\_film) "The Chase (1966 film)")_ (1966),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Thoroughly Modern Millie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughly\_Modern\_Millie "Thoroughly Modern Millie")_ (1967),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Isadora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isadora\_(film) "Isadora (film)")_ (1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (1970).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)

### Spiritual life and break from acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Spiritual life and break from acting")]

After finishing work on _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (released 1970, but shot in 1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) Fox suspended his acting career. The film, which starred Fox and [Mick Jagger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Jagger "Mick Jagger"), was deemed so outrageous that critics at a preview screening walked out, with one film executive's wife reportedly throwing up in the cinema.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)

In a 2008 interview, Fox said: "It was just part of my journey...I think my journey was to spend a while away from acting. And I never lost contact with it – watching movies, reading about it ... so I didn't feel I missed it."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tweed-10)

Fox became an evangelical Christian, working with the [Navigators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Navigators_(organization) "The Navigators (organization)") and devoting himself to the ministry.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cinema-11) During this time, the only film in which Fox appeared was _No Longer Alone_ (1976), the story of Joan Winmill Brown,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12) a suicidal woman who was led to faith in [Jesus Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Christ "Jesus Christ") by [Ruth Bell Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Bell_Graham "Ruth Bell Graham").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12)

### Return to acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Return to acting")]

After an absence from acting of several years, in 1981 Fox appeared on television in the _[Play for Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play\_for\_Today "Play for Today")_ "Country" by [Trevor Griffiths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Griffiths "Trevor Griffiths"), a comedy drama set against the 1945 UK parliamentary elections. On film he starred in [Stephen Poliakoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Poliakoff "Stephen Poliakoff")'s _[Runners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runners\_(film) "Runners (film)")_ (1983),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _[Comrades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comrades\_(1986\_film) "Comrades (1986 film)")_ (1986).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He played [Anthony Blunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Blunt "Anthony Blunt") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") play by [Alan Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Bennett "Alan Bennett"), _[A Question of Attribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Question\_of\_Attribution "A Question of Attribution")_ (1992).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He also portrayed the character of Lord Holmes in _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games "Patriot Games")_ (1992), as well as Colonel Ferguson in _[Farewell to the King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell\_to\_the\_King "Farewell to the King")_ (1989) and the Nazi-sympathising aristocrat Lord Darlington in _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993).

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Fox married Mary Elizabeth Piper in September 1973, with whom he has five children, including [Laurence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Fox "Laurence Fox") and [Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Fox_(actor) "Jack Fox (actor)"). Piper died at their home on 19 April 2020.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-foxes-2)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-telegraph_241195-15)

Through his daughter Lydia, Fox's son-in-law is actor [Richard Ayoade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Ayoade "Richard Ayoade").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-telegraph_20170623-16) His former daughter-in-law is actress [Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper"), who was married to his son Laurence from 2007 to 2016.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-BBC_News-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-itv_20160512-18)

_**Absolute Beginners**_ is a 1986 British musical film adapted from [Colin MacInnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_MacInnes "Colin MacInnes")' [book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(novel) "Absolute Beginners (novel)") about life in late 1950s [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), directed by [Julien Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple "Julien Temple"). The film stars Eddie O' Connell, [Patsy Kensit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patsy_Kensit "Patsy Kensit"), James Fox, [Edward Tudor-Pole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Tudor-Pole "Edward Tudor-Pole"), [Anita Morris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Morris "Anita Morris"), and [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie"), with featured appearances by [Sade Adu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sade_(singer) "Sade (singer)"), [Ray Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Davies "Ray Davies"), and [Steven Berkoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Berkoff "Steven Berkoff"). It was screened out of competition at the [1986 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Cannes_Film_Festival "1986 Cannes Film Festival").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-festival-cannes.com-4) It received coverage in the British media but was panned by critics and became a box office failure, although modern reviews have been more favourable.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-5) Bowie's [theme song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(David_Bowie_song) "Absolute Beginners (David Bowie song)") was very popular in the UK, spending nine weeks on the charts and peaking at number two.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-6) The commercial failure of _Absolute Beginners_ and two other films is blamed for the collapse of British film studio [Goldcrest Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldcrest_Films "Goldcrest Films")[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-7) and for [Virgin Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Films "Virgin Films") withdrawing from production.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-al-8)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Taking place in 1958, [popular culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_culture "Popular culture") in London is transforming from 1950s [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") to a new generation on the verge of the [rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") 1960s. Young [photographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photographer "Photographer") Colin is in love with aspiring [fashion designer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion_designer "Fashion designer") Suzette. Colin aims to be an artist with integrity. Suzette's boss, famous designer Henley of [Mayfair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayfair "Mayfair"), takes advantage of her forward-thinking designs to boost his own image.

Colin lives in the poor, ethnically diverse neighbourhood of [Notting Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notting_Hill "Notting Hill"). To make money, he gets a job with music producer Harry Charms, taking photos of new [teen idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_idol "Teen idol") Baby Boom. Despite Colin getting commercial photography work, Suzette breaks up with him. She explains that she wants a successful and luxurious life, and won't settle for less ("Having It All"). Colin is initially despondent, but believes she'll eventually come back to him.

Colin learns that Suzette will be at a party hosted by [gossip columnist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gossip_columnist "Gossip columnist") Dido Lament, and so he attends. He learns Suzette plans to marry the middle-aged, [homosexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexual "Homosexual") Henley for her career ("Selling Out"). Colin also meets advertising mogul Vendice Partners at the party.

Meanwhile, the [Teddy Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teddy_Boy "Teddy Boy") subculture is increasingly hostile towards [Black residents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_British_people "Black British people") in London, spurred by the recent [rise in immigration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign-born_population_of_the_United_Kingdom "Foreign-born population of the United Kingdom"). The [White Defence League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Defence_League "White Defence League"), led by the Fanatic, preaches [fascist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fascism "Fascism") politics and is vehemently against the increasing ethnic diversity of London. Colin despises this racist ideology.

Partners brings Colin to his [advertising agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertising_agency "Advertising agency"), where he shows off plans for the White [Housing Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Housing_estate "Housing estate"). Partners offers Colin a position as an advertisement photographer. While hesitant at first, Colin takes the job in the hopes that money may help him win back Suzette ("That's Motivation").

Henley and Suzette marry, but she is deeply unhappy. Colin, Dido, and Charms go on the TV show _Searchlight_. Dido [gropes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groping "Groping") Colin, prompting him to have an outbust and rail against the elder generation trying to exploit teenagers. Later, at a jazz club, Colin is commended for his honesty on television. However, he's upset when he sees a newspaper headline about Suzette's wedding ("Killer Blow").

Racial violence intensifies in the area. Colin's Black friend, Mr. Cool, informs him that the racists are becoming more organized and dangerous. Colin discovers that the new White Housing Development is a scheme between Partners and Henley to "[redevelop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gentrification "Gentrification")" the "[West 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W_postcode_area "W postcode area")." Colin sends incriminating photos to Dido in an attempt to reveal the plan, but she's in cahoots with Partners and is no help.

Colin witnesses the 1958 [Notting Hill race riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notting_Hill_race_riots "Notting Hill race riots") ("Riot City"). His pleas for peace are ignored. The police eventually arrive and stop the violence. Colin finds Suzette and they flee a fire set by the WDL. Mr. Cool has a fight with Flikker and wins. There is celebratory dancing in the street as rain puts out the fires. Colin and Suzette go back to his flat and have sex. He throws her wedding ring out the window.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

The novel was admired by Don MacPherson, a magazine editor who was friends with Julien Temple, then best known for directing music videos. MacPherson, Temple and Temple's business partner Michael Hamlyn agreed to try to turn _Absolute Beginners_ into a film. MacPherson wrote the first draft, but this was not well received. Richard Burridge wrote a draft which was more positively received. The movie was going to be made at Virgin Films. Goldcrest Films also became involved as did Steve Woolley's Palace Flms.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-9)

According to a history of Palace Pictures "The main reason for Palace's commitment to Temple's film... was the tremendous depth of Powell's and Woolley's shared ambition. Here was a film that was clearly going to be a huge event, and Palace's partners were equally determined to be at the forefront of such a national spectacle. To say 'No' to _Absolute Beginners_ was unthinkable."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-10)

Temple later admitted "MacInnes's book has a very flawed narrative to my mind, and is very hard to adapt. It lacks drive in terms of plot, and largely concerns the central characters views on the world, about jazz, pop stars, television, advertising and so on."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-11)

Palace covered development costs. Under the arrangement between Palace and Goldcrest, the latter would provide 60% of the budget if Palace could find the other 40%. Palace raised this from Orion Pictures in the US. Eventually $2.5 million of the film's budget came from Orion and £2.5 million from Goldcrest. Goldcrest guaranteed any cost overruns[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-room-12)

Christopher Wicking was hired to do a version of the script which he said "had some sort of propulsion from one scene to the next".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-chris-13) He says the script helped raise American finance but then Julien Temple disregarded a lot of Wicking's ideas. Wicking also says the filmmakers could never decide if the musical numbers should advance the story or illustrate something about the characters at the time.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-chris-13)

Terry Johnson did a rewrite of the script. According to Sandy Lieberson of Goldcrest the script "was never nailed down, and it kept being edited and not edited during the whole run-up to production and during the production itself."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-14)

Eddie O'Connell and Patsy Kensit were relative unknowns when cast for the film and, according to Julien Temple in a 2016 interview (included on the re-released DVD/Blu-Ray), neither got on with each other pretty well. Temple wanted to include musicians that represented music from the 1950s through to the 1980s with many of his contacts being from music videos whom he had directed. Ed Tudor-Pole (playing teddyboy 'Ed The Ted') had met Temple through his work on _The Great Rock 'N' Roll Swindle_. Ray Davies, Sade and David Bowie were recruited after Temple had directed music videos for them ("[Predictable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predictable_(The_Kinks_song) "Predictable (The Kinks song)")" for Davies' group The Kinks in 1981, "[Hang On to Your Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hang_On_to_Your_Love "Hang On to Your Love")" and "[Smooth Operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_Operator "Smooth Operator")" for Sade in 1984 and the short film _[Jazzin' for Blue Jean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazzin'\_for\_Blue\_Jean "Jazzin' for Blue Jean")_ for Bowie also in 1984). Broadway star Anita Morris had appeared in Temple's promo for The Rolling Stones' "[She Was Hot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She_Was_Hot "She Was Hot")" whilst Eve Ferret had co-starred as a receptionist in _Jazzin' for Blue Jean_.

In the aforementioned 2016 interview, producer Stephen Woolley recalled the financial challenges that were facing film company Goldcrest at the time- _Absolute Beginners_ was made around the same time as [Hugh Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Hudson "Hugh Hudson")'s _[Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolution\_(1985\_film) "Revolution (1985 film)")_ (starring [Al Pacino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Pacino "Al Pacino")) and [Roland Joffé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland_Joff%C3%A9 "Roland Joffé")'s _[The Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mission\_(1986\_film) "The Mission (1986 film)")_ (starring [Robert De Niro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_De_Niro "Robert De Niro") and [Jeremy Irons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Irons "Jeremy Irons")); as both films were seen to be more high profile due to their relatively higher budgets and more noted filmstars, _Absolute Beginners_ did not get as much financial support the other two films. All three films would fail at the box office leading to Goldcrest's eventual collapse.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-ink-15)

The cost of the film blew out during filming, rising from £6 million to £8.6 million. Alan Marshall was hired to oversee the project through to completion.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-16) Goldcrest wound up having to invest £5 million.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-17)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Release")]

Angus Finney, in his history of Palace Films, wrote the movie "is perhaps best remembered as an extraordinary British marketing phenomenon. An enormous party was held by Palace inside the railings of Leicester Square. Newspapers, magazines, cartoons, radio chat shows, a South Bank television special, and all other ways of promoting the movie were pursued relentlessly. Phil Symes and Angie Errigo worked long hours to ensure the film maximum publicity coverage."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-18) According to Jack Eberts of Goldcrest "probably no film has been so over-promoted in the history of the British film business. The expectations of the audience were raised to such heights that the picture could only suffer by comparison."[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-19)

Whilst the critical reviews in the UK were fairly disappointing, the box office performed respectably well whilst the reverse was true in America, where good notices by critics were not matched by a number of ticket sales. Temple would note in 2016 that he had to leave the UK in order to find work elsewhere- two noted fans of the film were Michael and Janet Jackson, leading to him directing Janet's promo clips for "When I Think Of You" and "Alright" which emulate some of the visual style of _Absolute Beginners_. Other musicians like Bowie, [Billy Idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Idol "Billy Idol"), [Whitney Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitney_Houston "Whitney Houston") and [Blur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blur_(band) "Blur (band)") (amongst others) would keep Temple's career in music video directing ongoing.

The film had its premiere at the [Leicester Square Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odeon_Luxe_West_End "Odeon Luxe West End") on 3 April 1986 attended by [Princess Anne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princess_Anne "Princess Anne").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-20) It opened to the public the following day at the theatre and at the [Odeon Marble Arch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odeon_Marble_Arch "Odeon Marble Arch") before expanding nationwide on 11 April.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-21)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Critical response")]

_[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ film critic [Caryn James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caryn_James "Caryn James") remarked upon the "unevenness" of Temple's adaptation and its "erratic" results.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-James-22)[Pauline Kael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_Kael "Pauline Kael") declared that the music was "peculiarly unlyrical and ephemeral".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-Kael-23) Jeremy Allen in _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ praised Bowie's theme song but described the film as "an overbudget turkey of huge proportions".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-24) Corey K. Creekmur stated in _The International Film Musical_ that the film "failed to deliver on the critical expectations surrounding it", although it remained "a deeply interesting, if flawed, attempt to harness the contemporary musical in the services of politics and social equality".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-25)

Alex Stewart reviewed _Absolute Beginners_ for _[White Dwarf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Dwarf\_(magazine) "White Dwarf (magazine)")_ #79, and stated that "It's glossy, slick and superficial, with a couple of nods towards Social Significance which stand out almost as awkwardly as the stumps of the subplots that ended up on the cutting-room floor. On the other hand the singing and dancing are quite nice, the climax looks uncannily like _Quatermass and the Pit_ set to music, and the grossly over-hyped Patsy Kensit duly meets a most satisfying nemesis by turning in a performance that would have disgraced an episode of _Thunderbirds_."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-WD79-26)

_Absolute Beginners_ currently holds a 73% rating on [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), based on 11 reviews.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-27) Audiences polled by [CinemaScore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScore "CinemaScore") gave the film an average grade of "B+" on an A+ to F scale.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-28)

_Filmink_ argued "there's so much great stuff and talent on display and it's a lot of fun. It just cost far, far too much money (like, four times what it needed to), it screws up its central love story, and had a male lead actor who couldn't sing, dance or act."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-al-8)

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Box office")]

The film earned £500,000 in rentals in the UK and $300,000 in the US. Goldcrest Films invested £4,680,000 in the film and received £1,859,000 back, losing £2,821,000.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-29)

According to Jake Eberts "The whole exercise had been a disaster. At every stage, from the original conception, through the script, the pre-production, production and post-production, to the marketing and distribution. _Absolute Beginners_ was an object lesson in how not to produce a movie."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-30)

## Soundtrack

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Soundtrack")]

_Absolute Beginners: The Original Motion Picture Soundtrack_ was concurrently released to promote the film, and the musical score was composed by [Gil Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gil_Evans "Gil Evans"). David Bowie's title track, Ray Davies' "Quiet Life", and [the Style Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Style_Council "The Style Council")'s "Have You Ever Had It Blue?" were released as singles. Abridged versions of the LP were released featuring only sides one and two, and CD versions excised the tracks "Absolute Beginners (Slight Refrain)," "Landlords and Tenants", "Santa Lucia". and "Cool Napoli".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

_**Absolute Beginners**_ is a 1986 British musical film adapted from [Colin MacInnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_MacInnes "Colin MacInnes")' [book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(novel) "Absolute Beginners (novel)") about life in late 1950s [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), directed by [Julien Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple "Julien Temple"). The film stars Eddie O' Connell, [Patsy Kensit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patsy_Kensit "Patsy Kensit"), James Fox, [Edward Tudor-Pole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Tudor-Pole "Edward Tudor-Pole"), [Anita Morris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Morris "Anita Morris"), and [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie"), with featured appearances by [Sade Adu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sade_(singer) "Sade (singer)"), [Ray Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Davies "Ray Davies"), and [Steven Berkoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Berkoff "Steven Berkoff"). It was screened out of competition at the [1986 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Cannes_Film_Festival "1986 Cannes Film Festival").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-festival-cannes.com-4) It received coverage in the British media but was panned by critics and became a box office failure, although modern reviews have been more favourable.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-5) Bowie's [theme song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(David_Bowie_song) "Absolute Beginners (David Bowie song)") was very popular in the UK, spending nine weeks on the charts and peaking at number two.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-6) The commercial failure of _Absolute Beginners_ and two other films is blamed for the collapse of British film studio [Goldcrest Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldcrest_Films "Goldcrest Films")[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-7) and for [Virgin Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Films "Virgin Films") withdrawing from production.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-al-8)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Taking place in 1958, [popular culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_culture "Popular culture") in London is transforming from 1950s [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") to a new generation on the verge of the [rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") 1960s. Young [photographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photographer "Photographer") Colin is in love with aspiring [fashion designer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion_designer "Fashion designer") Suzette. Colin aims to be an artist with integrity. Suzette's boss, famous designer Henley of [Mayfair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayfair "Mayfair"), takes advantage of her forward-thinking designs to boost his own image.

Colin lives in the poor, ethnically diverse neighbourhood of [Notting Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notting_Hill "Notting Hill"). To make money, he gets a job with music producer Harry Charms, taking photos of new [teen idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_idol "Teen idol") Baby Boom. Despite Colin getting commercial photography work, Suzette breaks up with him. She explains that she wants a successful and luxurious life, and won't settle for less ("Having It All"). Colin is initially despondent, but believes she'll eventually come back to him.

Colin learns that Suzette will be at a party hosted by [gossip columnist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gossip_columnist "Gossip columnist") Dido Lament, and so he attends. He learns Suzette plans to marry the middle-aged, [homosexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexual "Homosexual") Henley for her career ("Selling Out"). Colin also meets advertising mogul Vendice Partners at the party.

Meanwhile, the [Teddy Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teddy_Boy "Teddy Boy") subculture is increasingly hostile towards [Black residents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_British_people "Black British people") in London, spurred by the recent [rise in immigration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign-born_population_of_the_United_Kingdom "Foreign-born population of the United Kingdom"). The [White Defence League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Defence_League "White Defence League"), led by the Fanatic, preaches [fascist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fascism "Fascism") politics and is vehemently against the increasing ethnic diversity of London. Colin despises this racist ideology.

Partners brings Colin to his [advertising agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertising_agency "Advertising agency"), where he shows off plans for the White [Housing Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Housing_estate "Housing estate"). Partners offers Colin a position as an advertisement photographer. While hesitant at first, Colin takes the job in the hopes that money may help him win back Suzette ("That's Motivation").

Henley and Suzette marry, but she is deeply unhappy. Colin, Dido, and Charms go on the TV show _Searchlight_. Dido [gropes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groping "Groping") Colin, prompting him to have an outbust and rail against the elder generation trying to exploit teenagers. Later, at a jazz club, Colin is commended for his honesty on television. However, he's upset when he sees a newspaper headline about Suzette's wedding ("Killer Blow").

Racial violence intensifies in the area. Colin's Black friend, Mr. Cool, informs him that the racists are becoming more organized and dangerous. Colin discovers that the new White Housing Development is a scheme between Partners and Henley to "[redevelop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gentrification "Gentrification")" the "[West 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W_postcode_area "W postcode area")." Colin sends incriminating photos to Dido in an attempt to reveal the plan, but she's in cahoots with Partners and is no help.

Colin witnesses the 1958 [Notting Hill race riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notting_Hill_race_riots "Notting Hill race riots") ("Riot City"). His pleas for peace are ignored. The police eventually arrive and stop the violence. Colin finds Suzette and they flee a fire set by the WDL. Mr. Cool has a fight with Flikker and wins. There is celebratory dancing in the street as rain puts out the fires. Colin and Suzette go back to his flat and have sex. He throws her wedding ring out the window.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

The novel was admired by Don MacPherson, a magazine editor who was friends with Julien Temple, then best known for directing music videos. MacPherson, Temple and Temple's business partner Michael Hamlyn agreed to try to turn _Absolute Beginners_ into a film. MacPherson wrote the first draft, but this was not well received. Richard Burridge wrote a draft which was more positively received. The movie was going to be made at Virgin Films. Goldcrest Films also became involved as did Steve Woolley's Palace Flms.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-9)

According to a history of Palace Pictures "The main reason for Palace's commitment to Temple's film... was the tremendous depth of Powell's and Woolley's shared ambition. Here was a film that was clearly going to be a huge event, and Palace's partners were equally determined to be at the forefront of such a national spectacle. To say 'No' to _Absolute Beginners_ was unthinkable."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-10)

Temple later admitted "MacInnes's book has a very flawed narrative to my mind, and is very hard to adapt. It lacks drive in terms of plot, and largely concerns the central characters views on the world, about jazz, pop stars, television, advertising and so on."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-11)

Palace covered development costs. Under the arrangement between Palace and Goldcrest, the latter would provide 60% of the budget if Palace could find the other 40%. Palace raised this from Orion Pictures in the US. Eventually $2.5 million of the film's budget came from Orion and £2.5 million from Goldcrest. Goldcrest guaranteed any cost overruns[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-room-12)

Christopher Wicking was hired to do a version of the script which he said "had some sort of propulsion from one scene to the next".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-chris-13) He says the script helped raise American finance but then Julien Temple disregarded a lot of Wicking's ideas. Wicking also says the filmmakers could never decide if the musical numbers should advance the story or illustrate something about the characters at the time.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-chris-13)

Terry Johnson did a rewrite of the script. According to Sandy Lieberson of Goldcrest the script "was never nailed down, and it kept being edited and not edited during the whole run-up to production and during the production itself."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-14)

Eddie O'Connell and Patsy Kensit were relative unknowns when cast for the film and, according to Julien Temple in a 2016 interview (included on the re-released DVD/Blu-Ray), neither got on with each other pretty well. Temple wanted to include musicians that represented music from the 1950s through to the 1980s with many of his contacts being from music videos whom he had directed. Ed Tudor-Pole (playing teddyboy 'Ed The Ted') had met Temple through his work on _The Great Rock 'N' Roll Swindle_. Ray Davies, Sade and David Bowie were recruited after Temple had directed music videos for them ("[Predictable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predictable_(The_Kinks_song) "Predictable (The Kinks song)")" for Davies' group The Kinks in 1981, "[Hang On to Your Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hang_On_to_Your_Love "Hang On to Your Love")" and "[Smooth Operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_Operator "Smooth Operator")" for Sade in 1984 and the short film _[Jazzin' for Blue Jean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazzin'\_for\_Blue\_Jean "Jazzin' for Blue Jean")_ for Bowie also in 1984). Broadway star Anita Morris had appeared in Temple's promo for The Rolling Stones' "[She Was Hot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She_Was_Hot "She Was Hot")" whilst Eve Ferret had co-starred as a receptionist in _Jazzin' for Blue Jean_.

In the aforementioned 2016 interview, producer Stephen Woolley recalled the financial challenges that were facing film company Goldcrest at the time- _Absolute Beginners_ was made around the same time as [Hugh Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Hudson "Hugh Hudson")'s _[Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolution\_(1985\_film) "Revolution (1985 film)")_ (starring [Al Pacino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Pacino "Al Pacino")) and [Roland Joffé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland_Joff%C3%A9 "Roland Joffé")'s _[The Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mission\_(1986\_film) "The Mission (1986 film)")_ (starring [Robert De Niro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_De_Niro "Robert De Niro") and [Jeremy Irons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Irons "Jeremy Irons")); as both films were seen to be more high profile due to their relatively higher budgets and more noted filmstars, _Absolute Beginners_ did not get as much financial support the other two films. All three films would fail at the box office leading to Goldcrest's eventual collapse.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-ink-15)

The cost of the film blew out during filming, rising from £6 million to £8.6 million. Alan Marshall was hired to oversee the project through to completion.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-16) Goldcrest wound up having to invest £5 million.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-17)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Release")]

Angus Finney, in his history of Palace Films, wrote the movie "is perhaps best remembered as an extraordinary British marketing phenomenon. An enormous party was held by Palace inside the railings of Leicester Square. Newspapers, magazines, cartoons, radio chat shows, a South Bank television special, and all other ways of promoting the movie were pursued relentlessly. Phil Symes and Angie Errigo worked long hours to ensure the film maximum publicity coverage."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-18) According to Jack Eberts of Goldcrest "probably no film has been so over-promoted in the history of the British film business. The expectations of the audience were raised to such heights that the picture could only suffer by comparison."[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-19)

Whilst the critical reviews in the UK were fairly disappointing, the box office performed respectably well whilst the reverse was true in America, where good notices by critics were not matched by a number of ticket sales. Temple would note in 2016 that he had to leave the UK in order to find work elsewhere- two noted fans of the film were Michael and Janet Jackson, leading to him directing Janet's promo clips for "When I Think Of You" and "Alright" which emulate some of the visual style of _Absolute Beginners_. Other musicians like Bowie, [Billy Idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Idol "Billy Idol"), [Whitney Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitney_Houston "Whitney Houston") and [Blur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blur_(band) "Blur (band)") (amongst others) would keep Temple's career in music video directing ongoing.

The film had its premiere at the [Leicester Square Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odeon_Luxe_West_End "Odeon Luxe West End") on 3 April 1986 attended by [Princess Anne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princess_Anne "Princess Anne").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-20) It opened to the public the following day at the theatre and at the [Odeon Marble Arch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odeon_Marble_Arch "Odeon Marble Arch") before expanding nationwide on 11 April.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-21)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Critical response")]

_[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ film critic [Caryn James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caryn_James "Caryn James") remarked upon the "unevenness" of Temple's adaptation and its "erratic" results.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-James-22)[Pauline Kael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_Kael "Pauline Kael") declared that the music was "peculiarly unlyrical and ephemeral".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-Kael-23) Jeremy Allen in _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ praised Bowie's theme song but described the film as "an overbudget turkey of huge proportions".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-24) Corey K. Creekmur stated in _The International Film Musical_ that the film "failed to deliver on the critical expectations surrounding it", although it remained "a deeply interesting, if flawed, attempt to harness the contemporary musical in the services of politics and social equality".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-25)

Alex Stewart reviewed _Absolute Beginners_ for _[White Dwarf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Dwarf\_(magazine) "White Dwarf (magazine)")_ #79, and stated that "It's glossy, slick and superficial, with a couple of nods towards Social Significance which stand out almost as awkwardly as the stumps of the subplots that ended up on the cutting-room floor. On the other hand the singing and dancing are quite nice, the climax looks uncannily like _Quatermass and the Pit_ set to music, and the grossly over-hyped Patsy Kensit duly meets a most satisfying nemesis by turning in a performance that would have disgraced an episode of _Thunderbirds_."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-WD79-26)

_Absolute Beginners_ currently holds a 73% rating on [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), based on 11 reviews.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-27) Audiences polled by [CinemaScore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScore "CinemaScore") gave the film an average grade of "B+" on an A+ to F scale.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-28)

_Filmink_ argued "there's so much great stuff and talent on display and it's a lot of fun. It just cost far, far too much money (like, four times what it needed to), it screws up its central love story, and had a male lead actor who couldn't sing, dance or act."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-al-8)

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Box office")]

The film earned £500,000 in rentals in the UK and $300,000 in the US. Goldcrest Films invested £4,680,000 in the film and received £1,859,000 back, losing £2,821,000.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-29)

According to Jake Eberts "The whole exercise had been a disaster. At every stage, from the original conception, through the script, the pre-production, production and post-production, to the marketing and distribution. _Absolute Beginners_ was an object lesson in how not to produce a movie."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Beginners_(film)#cite_note-30)

## Soundtrack

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Absolute_Beginners_(film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Soundtrack")]

_Absolute Beginners: The Original Motion Picture Soundtrack_ was concurrently released to promote the film, and the musical score was composed by [Gil Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gil_Evans "Gil Evans"). David Bowie's title track, Ray Davies' "Quiet Life", and [the Style Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Style_Council "The Style Council")'s "Have You Ever Had It Blue?" were released as singles. Abridged versions of the LP were released featuring only sides one and two, and CD versions excised the tracks "Absolute Beginners (Slight Refrain)," "Landlords and Tenants", "Santa Lucia". and "Cool Napoli".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

**Julien Temple** (born 26 November 1953) is a British film, documentary and music video director.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-NYT-1) He began his career with short films featuring the [Sex Pistols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_Pistols "Sex Pistols"), and has continued with various off-beat projects, including _[The Great Rock 'n' Roll Swindle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_Rock\_'n'\_Roll\_Swindle "The Great Rock 'n' Roll Swindle")_,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-NYT-1)_[Absolute Beginners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute\_Beginners\_(film) "Absolute Beginners (film)")_ and a documentary film about _[Glastonbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glastonbury\_(film) "Glastonbury (film)")_.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julien_Temple&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Temple was born in Kensington, London, the son of Landon Temple, who organised the travel company Progressive Tours.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-2) He was educated at [St Marylebone Grammar School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Marylebone_Grammar_School "St Marylebone Grammar School") (from which he was expelled), [William Ellis School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Ellis_School "William Ellis School"), and [King's College, Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's_College,_Cambridge "King's College, Cambridge").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-3) He grew up with little interest in film until, when a student at Cambridge, he discovered the works of French anarchist director [Jean Vigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Vigo "Jean Vigo"). This, along with his interest in the early [punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") scene in London in 1976, led to his friendship with [The Sex Pistols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sex_Pistols "The Sex Pistols"), leading him to document many of their early gigs.

### 1970s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julien_Temple&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1970s")]

Temple's first film was a short [documentary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Documentary_film "Documentary film") called _Sex Pistols Number 1_, which set out to show the rise of the band from 1976 to 1977, in a series of short clips from television interviews and gigs. This led to Temple making _[The Great Rock And Roll Swindle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_Rock\_And\_Roll\_Swindle "The Great Rock And Roll Swindle")_, another documentary. As band members [Johnny Rotten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Rotten "Johnny Rotten") and [Sid Vicious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sid_Vicious "Sid Vicious") had left the band by this time, the story of the group is told from the viewpoint of their [manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talent_manager "Talent manager"), [Malcolm McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_McLaren "Malcolm McLaren").

_The Great Rock And Roll Swindle_ tells of the rise of The Sex Pistols, apparently as manipulated by McLaren, and how he had shaped the band throughout their short career. Many of the 'facts' given by McLaren were disputed by John Lydon (who had dropped the Johnny Rotten name after leaving the band), who accused McLaren of using the film to attack him personally. This helped split opinion on the film as, although it was praised for attempting to capture some of the punk scene of the time, it was seen as too skewed towards McLaren's vision. Controversy aside, Temple was praised[_[by whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Words\_to\_watch#Unsupported\_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_] for his mix of animated scenes, documentary footage, and specially shot footage which he used to tell McLaren's story. This helped launch Temple into a career making [music videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video"), something for which he would be best known for much of his career.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-al-4)

### 1980s and 1990s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julien_Temple&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1980s and 1990s")]

In 1983, Temple directed a film for the BBC [Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena_(UK_TV_series) "Arena (UK TV series)") series called _[It's All True](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's\_All\_True\_(BBC\_Film)?action=edit&redlink=1 "It's All True (BBC Film) (page does not exist)")_, named after the 1942 unfinished [Orson Welles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orson_Welles "Orson Welles") film. [Compered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Ceremonies "Master of Ceremonies") by Welles himself, the film comprised many short segments about the state of the video industry, both real and imagined, many featuring cameos by celebrities including [Mel Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Brooks "Mel Brooks"), [Grace Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace_Jones "Grace Jones"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-5)[Ray Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Davies "Ray Davies"), and [Koo Stark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koo_Stark "Koo Stark").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-6) This was followed by Temple's next theatrical release, the short film _[Jazzin' for Blue Jean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazzin'\_for\_Blue\_Jean "Jazzin' for Blue Jean")_ featuring [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie") which was released as a support feature to _[The Company of Wolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Company\_of\_Wolves "The Company of Wolves")_. By 1985, Temple was now well known for being a director of successful music videos by the Kinks, The Rolling Stones, David Bowie and other British artists, several of which were early, groundbreaking, videos for the new MTV channel, but he was yet to direct a major film.

In 1986, Temple directed the film version of [Colin MacInnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_MacInnes "Colin MacInnes")' book _[Absolute Beginners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute\_Beginners\_(film) "Absolute Beginners (film)")_. One of the most expensive films in British history, the fate of the [studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_British_film_studios "List of British film studios") involved (as well as several careers) were dependent on the success of the film.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-al-4) The film was critically panned in the UK. As it was a musical, rather than a straight adaptation of the book, it was attacked for a lack of narrative; it was also called "a series of badly-linked music videos". _Absolute Beginners_ was financially unsuccessful and was partly responsible for the [Goldcrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldcrest_Films "Goldcrest Films") company going [bankrupt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bankruptcy_in_the_United_Kingdom "Bankruptcy in the United Kingdom"). Temple found himself being blamed personally for the failure. He moved to the United States, where he directed _[Earth Girls Are Easy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth\_Girls\_Are\_Easy "Earth Girls Are Easy")_, as well as a series of music videos for such artists as [Duran Duran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duran_Duran "Duran Duran"), [Janet Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Jackson "Janet Jackson"), [Neil Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Young "Neil Young") and [Tom Petty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Petty "Tom Petty"). He set up the Nitrate Film production company in 1986 with his wife, producer Amanda Temple.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-crockofgold_notes-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-variety-exec-8)

Temple returned to the UK in the late 1990s, where he continued to make films and music videos. _Vigo: Passion for Life_ (1998) recounts the passionate relationship between French film maker [Jean Vigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Vigo "Jean Vigo") (1905–34) and his wife Lydou, who both suffered from [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis "Tuberculosis").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-9) The film was not well received. A reviewer in _Sight & Sound_ commented that the film "although absolutely faithful to the facts, is absolutely dreadful".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-10)

### 2000s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julien_Temple&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2000s")]

Films which followed included _[Pandæmonium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandaemonium\_(film) "Pandaemonium (film)")_ (2001), a critically acclaimed film about the friendship between [Romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_poetry "Romantic poetry")[poets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poets "Poets")[Samuel Taylor Coleridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Taylor_Coleridge "Samuel Taylor Coleridge") and [William Wordsworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Wordsworth "William Wordsworth"), and _[The Filth and the Fury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Filth\_and\_the\_Fury "The Filth and the Fury")_ (2000), another documentary about The Sex Pistols. This time the film was made with the full cooperation of the surviving members of the band and told the story of the band from their viewpoint. This film mixed newly shot footage and interviews with footage culled from _The Great Rock and Roll Swindle_ and previously unseen interviews. The film was a critical success and was seen as setting the record straight in regard to the history of The Sex Pistols.

Between 2002 and 2005, Temple completed a feature-length documentary about the [Glastonbury Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glastonbury_Festival "Glastonbury Festival"). This involved him shooting footage at the festival as well as drawing on the vast amount of archival footage, as well as footage sent in by fans of the festival. It was released in the UK in April 2006.

In 2006, Temple made a film of the life of his friend, in _[Joe Strummer: The Future Is Unwritten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe\_Strummer:\_The\_Future\_Is\_Unwritten "Joe Strummer: The Future Is Unwritten")_. It premiered in January 2007.

In November 2007, Temple filmed several of the Sex Pistols' comeback shows at the Brixton Academy in London. This was followed by several filming sessions with each member of the band as they re-visited their old London haunts. The footage was assembled into a new documentary film released on DVD in 2008 as _The Sex Pistols: There'll Always Be An England_, bringing Temple's association with the Sex Pistols up to date.

In June 2008, Temple filmed three concerts by [Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madness_(band) "Madness (band)") at the [Hackney Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hackney_Empire "Hackney Empire"). These concerts were previews of the band's forthcoming album, _The Liberty of Norton Folgate_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-11)

In 2009, Temple directed the third film in his punk trilogy, _Oil City Confidential_, which celebrated the Canvey Island legends [Dr. Feelgood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Feelgood_(band) "Dr. Feelgood (band)"), and a hymn to the [Motor City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motor_City "Motor City") entitled _Requiem For Detroit?_ (2010).

### 2010s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julien_Temple&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2010s")]

In 2010, Temple directed the biography _Ray Davies: Imaginary Man_. Previously, he had directed several [Kinks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinks "Kinks") videos. Also, he was referred to by name in The Kinks song _Too Hot_ from their _Word of Mouth_ album: "Julien's on the street today/ Scouting out locations..."

In 2011, Temple returned to Glastonbury to further document the legendary festival. The resulting 75-minute film, titled _"Glastonbury After Hours: Glastopia"_, was shot on location in the Shangri-La, Arcadia, the Unfair Ground, Strummerville, Block 9 and the Common areas. It was premiered on BBC4 on 15 June 2012.

On 4 March 2013, it was announced that [Jesse L. Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_L._Martin "Jesse L. Martin") would replace [Lenny Kravitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenny_Kravitz "Lenny Kravitz") as [Marvin Gaye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Gaye "Marvin Gaye") in _Sexual Healing_, directed by Temple, and produced by Vassal Benton and Fred Bestall.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-abc-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-def-13) With approximately 70% of the film completed[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-auto-14) and only three weeks to go on a planned nine-and-a-half-week shoot, production was stopped on the biopic, primarily due to financial problems.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-15) (Crew members were said to have not been paid fully for their work on the film.)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-auto-14)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julien_Temple&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

With his wife, Amanda (Pirie) Temple,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-16) Temple has a daughter, the actress [Juno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Temple "Juno Temple"), and two sons.

His sister, [Nina Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nina_Temple "Nina Temple"), was the last General Secretary of the [Communist Party of Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_Great_Britain "Communist Party of Great Britain").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-17)
