**Julien Temple** (born 26 November 1953) is a British film, documentary and music video director.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-NYT-1) He began his career with short films featuring the [Sex Pistols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_Pistols "Sex Pistols"), and has continued with various off-beat projects, including _[The Great Rock 'n' Roll Swindle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_Rock\_'n'\_Roll\_Swindle "The Great Rock 'n' Roll Swindle")_,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-NYT-1)_[Absolute Beginners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute\_Beginners\_(film) "Absolute Beginners (film)")_ and a documentary film about _[Glastonbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glastonbury\_(film) "Glastonbury (film)")_.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julien_Temple&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Temple was born in Kensington, London, the son of Landon Temple, who organised the travel company Progressive Tours.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-2) He was educated at [St Marylebone Grammar School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Marylebone_Grammar_School "St Marylebone Grammar School") (from which he was expelled), [William Ellis School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Ellis_School "William Ellis School"), and [King's College, Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's_College,_Cambridge "King's College, Cambridge").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-3) He grew up with little interest in film until, when a student at Cambridge, he discovered the works of French anarchist director [Jean Vigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Vigo "Jean Vigo"). This, along with his interest in the early [punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") scene in London in 1976, led to his friendship with [The Sex Pistols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sex_Pistols "The Sex Pistols"), leading him to document many of their early gigs.

## Career

### 1970s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julien_Temple&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1970s")]

Temple's first film was a short [documentary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Documentary_film "Documentary film") called _Sex Pistols Number 1_, which set out to show the rise of the band from 1976 to 1977, in a series of short clips from television interviews and gigs. This led to Temple making _[The Great Rock And Roll Swindle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_Rock\_And\_Roll\_Swindle "The Great Rock And Roll Swindle")_, another documentary. As band members [Johnny Rotten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Rotten "Johnny Rotten") and [Sid Vicious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sid_Vicious "Sid Vicious") had left the band by this time, the story of the group is told from the viewpoint of their [manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talent_manager "Talent manager"), [Malcolm McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_McLaren "Malcolm McLaren").

_The Great Rock And Roll Swindle_ tells of the rise of The Sex Pistols, apparently as manipulated by McLaren, and how he had shaped the band throughout their short career. Many of the 'facts' given by McLaren were disputed by John Lydon (who had dropped the Johnny Rotten name after leaving the band), who accused McLaren of using the film to attack him personally. This helped split opinion on the film as, although it was praised for attempting to capture some of the punk scene of the time, it was seen as too skewed towards McLaren's vision. Controversy aside, Temple was praised[_[by whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Words\_to\_watch#Unsupported\_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_] for his mix of animated scenes, documentary footage, and specially shot footage which he used to tell McLaren's story. This helped launch Temple into a career making [music videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video"), something for which he would be best known for much of his career.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-al-4)

### 1980s and 1990s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julien_Temple&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1980s and 1990s")]

In 1983, Temple directed a film for the BBC [Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena_(UK_TV_series) "Arena (UK TV series)") series called _[It's All True](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's\_All\_True\_(BBC\_Film)?action=edit&redlink=1 "It's All True (BBC Film) (page does not exist)")_, named after the 1942 unfinished [Orson Welles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orson_Welles "Orson Welles") film. [Compered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Ceremonies "Master of Ceremonies") by Welles himself, the film comprised many short segments about the state of the video industry, both real and imagined, many featuring cameos by celebrities including [Mel Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Brooks "Mel Brooks"), [Grace Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace_Jones "Grace Jones"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-5)[Ray Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Davies "Ray Davies"), and [Koo Stark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koo_Stark "Koo Stark").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-6) This was followed by Temple's next theatrical release, the short film _[Jazzin' for Blue Jean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazzin'\_for\_Blue\_Jean "Jazzin' for Blue Jean")_ featuring [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie") which was released as a support feature to _[The Company of Wolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Company\_of\_Wolves "The Company of Wolves")_. By 1985, Temple was now well known for being a director of successful music videos by the Kinks, The Rolling Stones, David Bowie and other British artists, several of which were early, groundbreaking, videos for the new MTV channel, but he was yet to direct a major film.

In 1986, Temple directed the film version of [Colin MacInnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_MacInnes "Colin MacInnes")' book _[Absolute Beginners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute\_Beginners\_(film) "Absolute Beginners (film)")_. One of the most expensive films in British history, the fate of the [studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_British_film_studios "List of British film studios") involved (as well as several careers) were dependent on the success of the film.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-al-4) The film was critically panned in the UK. As it was a musical, rather than a straight adaptation of the book, it was attacked for a lack of narrative; it was also called "a series of badly-linked music videos". _Absolute Beginners_ was financially unsuccessful and was partly responsible for the [Goldcrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldcrest_Films "Goldcrest Films") company going [bankrupt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bankruptcy_in_the_United_Kingdom "Bankruptcy in the United Kingdom"). Temple found himself being blamed personally for the failure. He moved to the United States, where he directed _[Earth Girls Are Easy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth\_Girls\_Are\_Easy "Earth Girls Are Easy")_, as well as a series of music videos for such artists as [Duran Duran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duran_Duran "Duran Duran"), [Janet Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Jackson "Janet Jackson"), [Neil Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Young "Neil Young") and [Tom Petty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Petty "Tom Petty"). He set up the Nitrate Film production company in 1986 with his wife, producer Amanda Temple.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-crockofgold_notes-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-variety-exec-8)

Temple returned to the UK in the late 1990s, where he continued to make films and music videos. _Vigo: Passion for Life_ (1998) recounts the passionate relationship between French film maker [Jean Vigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Vigo "Jean Vigo") (1905–34) and his wife Lydou, who both suffered from [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis "Tuberculosis").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-9) The film was not well received. A reviewer in _Sight & Sound_ commented that the film "although absolutely faithful to the facts, is absolutely dreadful".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-10)

### 2000s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julien_Temple&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2000s")]

Films which followed included _[Pandæmonium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandaemonium\_(film) "Pandaemonium (film)")_ (2001), a critically acclaimed film about the friendship between [Romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_poetry "Romantic poetry")[poets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poets "Poets")[Samuel Taylor Coleridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Taylor_Coleridge "Samuel Taylor Coleridge") and [William Wordsworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Wordsworth "William Wordsworth"), and _[The Filth and the Fury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Filth\_and\_the\_Fury "The Filth and the Fury")_ (2000), another documentary about The Sex Pistols. This time the film was made with the full cooperation of the surviving members of the band and told the story of the band from their viewpoint. This film mixed newly shot footage and interviews with footage culled from _The Great Rock and Roll Swindle_ and previously unseen interviews. The film was a critical success and was seen as setting the record straight in regard to the history of The Sex Pistols.

Between 2002 and 2005, Temple completed a feature-length documentary about the [Glastonbury Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glastonbury_Festival "Glastonbury Festival"). This involved him shooting footage at the festival as well as drawing on the vast amount of archival footage, as well as footage sent in by fans of the festival. It was released in the UK in April 2006.

In 2006, Temple made a film of the life of his friend, in _[Joe Strummer: The Future Is Unwritten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe\_Strummer:\_The\_Future\_Is\_Unwritten "Joe Strummer: The Future Is Unwritten")_. It premiered in January 2007.

In November 2007, Temple filmed several of the Sex Pistols' comeback shows at the Brixton Academy in London. This was followed by several filming sessions with each member of the band as they re-visited their old London haunts. The footage was assembled into a new documentary film released on DVD in 2008 as _The Sex Pistols: There'll Always Be An England_, bringing Temple's association with the Sex Pistols up to date.

In June 2008, Temple filmed three concerts by [Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madness_(band) "Madness (band)") at the [Hackney Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hackney_Empire "Hackney Empire"). These concerts were previews of the band's forthcoming album, _The Liberty of Norton Folgate_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-11)

In 2009, Temple directed the third film in his punk trilogy, _Oil City Confidential_, which celebrated the Canvey Island legends [Dr. Feelgood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Feelgood_(band) "Dr. Feelgood (band)"), and a hymn to the [Motor City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motor_City "Motor City") entitled _Requiem For Detroit?_ (2010).

### 2010s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julien_Temple&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2010s")]

In 2010, Temple directed the biography _Ray Davies: Imaginary Man_. Previously, he had directed several [Kinks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinks "Kinks") videos. Also, he was referred to by name in The Kinks song _Too Hot_ from their _Word of Mouth_ album: "Julien's on the street today/ Scouting out locations..."

In 2011, Temple returned to Glastonbury to further document the legendary festival. The resulting 75-minute film, titled _"Glastonbury After Hours: Glastopia"_, was shot on location in the Shangri-La, Arcadia, the Unfair Ground, Strummerville, Block 9 and the Common areas. It was premiered on BBC4 on 15 June 2012.

On 4 March 2013, it was announced that [Jesse L. Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_L._Martin "Jesse L. Martin") would replace [Lenny Kravitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenny_Kravitz "Lenny Kravitz") as [Marvin Gaye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Gaye "Marvin Gaye") in _Sexual Healing_, directed by Temple, and produced by Vassal Benton and Fred Bestall.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-abc-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-def-13) With approximately 70% of the film completed[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-auto-14) and only three weeks to go on a planned nine-and-a-half-week shoot, production was stopped on the biopic, primarily due to financial problems.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-15) (Crew members were said to have not been paid fully for their work on the film.)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-auto-14)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julien_Temple&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

With his wife, Amanda (Pirie) Temple,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-16) Temple has a daughter, the actress [Juno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Temple "Juno Temple"), and two sons.

His sister, [Nina Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nina_Temple "Nina Temple"), was the last General Secretary of the [Communist Party of Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_Great_Britain "Communist Party of Great Britain").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple#cite_note-17)

**James William Fox** (born **William Fox**; 19 May 1939) is an English actor, known for his work in film and television. He is a member of the [Fox family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_family "Robin Fox family") of actors. Fox's career began in the 1960s through leading roles in films such as _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), _[King Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Rat\_(film) "King Rat (film)")_ (1965), _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ (1965), _[Thoroughly Modern Millie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughly\_Modern\_Millie "Thoroughly Modern Millie")_ (1967), and _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (1970).

In the 1970s, Fox took a break from acting to focus on personal and spiritual matters, returning to acting in the early 1980s. Over time, he built a reputation for playing a variety of roles, including upper-class figures and more serious characters, notably in known for his roles in _[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984), _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games\_(film) "Patriot Games (film)")_ (1992), _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993), _[Jinnah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinnah\_(film) "Jinnah (film)")_ (1998), _[Sherlock Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherlock\_Holmes\_(2009\_film) "Sherlock Holmes (2009 film)")_ (2009), and _[Effie Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effie\_Gray\_(film) "Effie Gray (film)")_ (2014).

Fox won the [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for his performance in _The Servant_, and was nominated for [Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role") for _A Passage to India_. He is also a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards") nominee.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

William Fox was born on 19 May 1939 in London, the second son of [theatrical agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_agent "Theatrical agent")[Robin Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-1) and actress Angela Worthington. His elder brother is actor [Edward Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Fox_(actor) "Edward Fox (actor)") and his younger brother was film producer [Robert Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Fox_(producer) "Robert Fox (producer)"). Fox's maternal grandfather was playwright [Frederick Lonsdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Lonsdale "Frederick Lonsdale").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-foxes-2) He applied successfully to study acting at the [Central School of Speech and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Central_School_of_Speech_and_Drama "Royal Central School of Speech and Drama").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-cssd-3)

## Career

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career")]

Fox first appeared on film as 11-year-old Toby Miniver in _[The Miniver Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Miniver\_Story "The Miniver Story")_ in 1950.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-acid-4) His early screen appearances, both in film and television, were made under his birth name, William Fox.

Fox appeared in the film _[The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Loneliness\_of\_the\_Long\_Distance\_Runner\_(film) "The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner (film)")_ (1962).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tv-5) His father, [Robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)"), quarrelled bitterly with [Tony Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Richardson "Tony Richardson") over this, having attempted to forbid his friend from giving his son James (known as "Willie") a part in the film. His father claimed Willie had no talent for acting and should not give up his job in a bank.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-6)

In 1964, Fox won a [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), working alongside [Dirk Bogarde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Bogarde "Dirk Bogarde"), [Sarah Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Miles "Sarah Miles"), and [Wendy Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Craig "Wendy Craig").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-bafta-1964-7) On 16 June 1965, [Ken Annakin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Annakin "Ken Annakin")'s period aviation film _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ was released. In this British [period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_film "Period film")[comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film"), Fox is featured among an international [ensemble cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensemble_cast "Ensemble cast") including [Stuart Whitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Whitman "Stuart Whitman"), Sarah Miles, [Robert Morley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Morley "Robert Morley"), [Terry-Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry-Thomas "Terry-Thomas"), [Red Skelton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Skelton "Red Skelton"), [Benny Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Hill "Benny Hill"), [Jean-Pierre Cassel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Pierre_Cassel "Jean-Pierre Cassel"), [Gert Fröbe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gert_Fr%C3%B6be "Gert Fröbe") and [Alberto Sordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Sordi "Alberto Sordi").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-nytimes_066838-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-variety_1200420712-9) (film)")_ (1970).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-acid-4)

### Spiritual life and break from acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Spiritual life and break from acting")]

After finishing work on _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (released 1970, but shot in 1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tv-5) Fox suspended his acting career. The film, which starred Fox and [Mick Jagger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Jagger "Mick Jagger"), was deemed so outrageous that critics at a preview screening walked out, with one film executive's wife reportedly throwing up in the cinema.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-acid-4)

In a 2008 interview, Fox said: "It was just part of my journey...I think my journey was to spend a while away from acting. And I never lost contact with it – watching movies, reading about it ... so I didn't feel I missed it."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tweed-10)

Fox became an evangelical Christian, working with the [Navigators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Navigators_(organization) "The Navigators (organization)") and devoting himself to the ministry.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-cinema-11) During this time, the only film in which Fox appeared was _No Longer Alone_ (1976), the story of Joan Winmill Brown,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-epit-12) a suicidal woman who was led to faith in [Jesus Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Christ "Jesus Christ") by [Ruth Bell Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Bell_Graham "Ruth Bell Graham").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-epit-12)

### Return to acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Return to acting")]

After an absence from acting of several years, in 1981 Fox appeared on television in the _[Play for Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play\_for\_Today "Play for Today")_ "Country" by [Trevor Griffiths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Griffiths "Trevor Griffiths"), a comedy drama set against the 1945 UK parliamentary elections. On film he starred in [Stephen Poliakoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Poliakoff "Stephen Poliakoff")'s _[Runners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runners\_(film) "Runners (film)")_ (1983),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tv-5)_[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tv-5) and _[Comrades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comrades\_(1986\_film) "Comrades (1986 film)")_ (1986).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tv-5) He played [Anthony Blunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Blunt "Anthony Blunt") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") play by [Alan Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Bennett "Alan Bennett"), _[A Question of Attribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Question\_of\_Attribution "A Question of Attribution")_ (1992).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tv-5) He also portrayed the character of Lord Holmes in _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games "Patriot Games")_ (1992), as well as Colonel Ferguson in _[Farewell to the King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell\_to\_the\_King "Farewell to the King")_ (1989) and the Nazi-sympathising aristocrat Lord Darlington in _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993).

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Fox married Mary Elizabeth Piper in September 1973, with whom he has five children, including [Laurence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Fox "Laurence Fox") and [Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Fox_(actor) "Jack Fox (actor)"). Piper died at their home on 19 April 2020.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-foxes-2)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-telegraph_241195-15)

Through his daughter Lydia, Fox's son-in-law is actor [Richard Ayoade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Ayoade "Richard Ayoade").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-telegraph_20170623-16) His former daughter-in-law is actress [Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper"), who was married to his son Laurence from 2007 to 2016.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-BBC_News-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-itv_20160512-18)

**James William Fox** (born **William Fox**; 19 May 1939) is an English actor, known for his work in film and television. He is a member of the [Fox family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_family "Robin Fox family") of actors. Fox's career began in the 1960s through leading roles in films such as _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), _[King Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Rat\_(film) "King Rat (film)")_ (1965), _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ (1965), _[Thoroughly Modern Millie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughly\_Modern\_Millie "Thoroughly Modern Millie")_ (1967), and _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (1970).

In the 1970s, Fox took a break from acting to focus on personal and spiritual matters, returning to acting in the early 1980s. Over time, he built a reputation for playing a variety of roles, including upper-class figures and more serious characters, notably in known for his roles in _[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984), _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games\_(film) "Patriot Games (film)")_ (1992), _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993), _[Jinnah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinnah\_(film) "Jinnah (film)")_ (1998), _[Sherlock Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherlock\_Holmes\_(2009\_film) "Sherlock Holmes (2009 film)")_ (2009), and _[Effie Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effie\_Gray\_(film) "Effie Gray (film)")_ (2014).

Fox won the [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for his performance in _The Servant_, and was nominated for [Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role") for _A Passage to India_. He is also a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards") nominee.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

William Fox was born on 19 May 1939 in London, the second son of [theatrical agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_agent "Theatrical agent")[Robin Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-1) and actress Angela Worthington. His elder brother is actor [Edward Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Fox_(actor) "Edward Fox (actor)") and his younger brother was film producer [Robert Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Fox_(producer) "Robert Fox (producer)"). Fox's maternal grandfather was playwright [Frederick Lonsdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Lonsdale "Frederick Lonsdale").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-foxes-2) He applied successfully to study acting at the [Central School of Speech and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Central_School_of_Speech_and_Drama "Royal Central School of Speech and Drama").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-cssd-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career")]

Fox first appeared on film as 11-year-old Toby Miniver in _[The Miniver Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Miniver\_Story "The Miniver Story")_ in 1950.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-acid-4) His early screen appearances, both in film and television, were made under his birth name, William Fox.

Fox appeared in the film _[The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Loneliness\_of\_the\_Long\_Distance\_Runner\_(film) "The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner (film)")_ (1962).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tv-5) His father, [Robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)"), quarrelled bitterly with [Tony Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Richardson "Tony Richardson") over this, having attempted to forbid his friend from giving his son James (known as "Willie") a part in the film. His father claimed Willie had no talent for acting and should not give up his job in a bank.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-6)

In 1964, Fox won a [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), working alongside [Dirk Bogarde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Bogarde "Dirk Bogarde"), [Sarah Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Miles "Sarah Miles"), and [Wendy Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Craig "Wendy Craig").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-bafta-1964-7) On 16 June 1965, [Ken Annakin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Annakin "Ken Annakin")'s period aviation film _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ was released. "Red Skelton"), [Benny Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Hill "Benny Hill"), [Jean-Pierre Cassel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Pierre_Cassel "Jean-Pierre Cassel"), [Gert ### Spiritual life and break from acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Spiritual life and break from acting")]

After finishing work on _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (released 1970, but shot in 1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tv-5) Fox suspended his acting career. The film, which starred Fox and [Mick Jagger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Jagger "Mick Jagger"), was deemed so outrageous that critics at a preview screening walked out, with one film executive's wife reportedly throwing up in the cinema.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-acid-4)

In a 2008 interview, Fox said: "It was just part of my journey...I think my journey was to spend a while away from acting. And I never lost contact with it – watching movies, reading about it ... so I didn't feel I missed it."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tweed-10)

Fox became an evangelical Christian, working with the [Navigators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Navigators_(organization) "The Navigators (organization)") and devoting himself to the ministry.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-cinema-11) During this time, the only film in which Fox appeared was _No Longer Alone_ (1976), the story of Joan Winmill Brown,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-epit-12) a suicidal woman who was led to faith in [Jesus Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Christ "Jesus Christ") by [Ruth Bell Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Bell_Graham "Ruth Bell Graham").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-epit-12)

### Return to acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Return to acting")]

After an absence from acting of several years, in 1981 Fox appeared on television in the _[Play for Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play\_for\_Today "Play for Today")_ "Country" by [Trevor Griffiths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Griffiths "Trevor Griffiths"), a comedy drama set against the 1945 UK parliamentary elections. On film he starred in [Stephen Poliakoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Poliakoff "Stephen Poliakoff")'s _[Runners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runners\_(film) "Runners (film)")_ (1983),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tv-5)_[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tv-5) and _[Comrades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comrades\_(1986\_film) "Comrades (1986 film)")_ (1986).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tv-5) He played [Anthony Blunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Blunt "Anthony Blunt") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") play by [Alan Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Bennett "Alan Bennett"), _[A Question of Attribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Question\_of\_Attribution "A Question of Attribution")_ (1992).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-tv-5) He also portrayed the character of Lord Holmes in _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games "Patriot Games")_ (1992), as well as Colonel Ferguson in _[Farewell to the King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell\_to\_the\_King "Farewell to the King")_ (1989) and the Nazi-sympathising aristocrat Lord Darlington in _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993).

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Fox married Mary Elizabeth Piper in September 1973, with whom he has five children, including [Laurence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Fox "Laurence Fox") and [Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Fox_(actor) "Jack Fox (actor)"). Piper died at their home on 19 April 2020.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-foxes-2)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-telegraph_241195-15)

Through his daughter Lydia, Fox's son-in-law is actor [Richard Ayoade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Ayoade "Richard Ayoade").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-telegraph_20170623-16) His former daughter-in-law is actress [Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper"), who was married to his son Laurence from 2007 to 2016.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-BBC_News-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&search=writer&fulltext=1#cite_note-itv_20160512-18)

1986 film by Peter Hyams

_**Running Scared**_ is a 1986 American [buddy cop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_cop_film "Buddy cop film")[action comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_comedy_film "Action comedy film") shot and directed by [Peter Hyams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams "Peter Hyams"), and written by [Gary Devore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_DeVore_(screenwriter) "Gary DeVore (screenwriter)") and Jimmy Huston. It stars [Gregory Hines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregory_Hines "Gregory Hines") and [Billy Crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Crystal "Billy Crystal") as two Chicago police officers who attempt to bring down a drug dealer before they retire.

The film was released by [MGM Entertainment Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MGM_Entertainment_Co. "MGM Entertainment Co.") on June 27, 1986. It received mixed reviews, with praise for the performances of Hines and Crystal, but criticism for its mix of action and comedy, and grossed over $38 million.

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Running_Scared_(1986_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Ray Hughes and Danny Costanzo are two police officers working on Chicago's North Side, known for their wisecracking demeanors and unorthodox police methods, which get results in their various cases. One such case involves trying to bust up-and-coming drug dealer Julio Gonzales when they discovered he was released from prison. After arresting Snake, one of Gonzales's associates, they convince him to [wear a wire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiretapping "Wiretapping") in order to get the necessary evidence to put Gonzales away. When they approach the meeting place (a cargo ship) they find that Gonzales has acquired a large store of Israeli [Uzi submachine guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzi "Uzi"). Snake is setting the detectives up, however, prompting the detectives to rush in by acting as though Gonzales was preparing to kill him. Gonzales reveals his ambition to be the Spanish "[Godfather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vito_Corleone "Vito Corleone")" of Chicago, but chastises Snake for letting the detectives get close, and Snake is shot dead by a subordinate. The pair look as though they will be killed, but two undercover detectives in Gonzales's gang step in to make the arrest. In the ensuing gun battle, most of the gang escape, but Ray and Danny capture Gonzales.

Back at the station Ray and Danny expect to be praised, but instead their captain chastises them for their sloppy work (as revealed by Snake's wire) and orders them to take a vacation. On vacation in [Key West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_West "Key West"), the pair develop a fondness for the laid-back and enjoyable atmosphere, and begin to question their career choice after the experience; when they discuss life after being cops, they decide to retire and open a bar.

When they return to Chicago and inform the captain of their intentions, they find out that Gonzales has been released and is free on bail. Incensed, they vow to capture Gonzales before retiring, but by being a little more careful in the process, requisitioning bulletproof vests they never considered before. To add insult to injury, Captain Logan assigns them the additional task of training their replacements before they go. They must train detectives Anthony Montoya and Frank Sigliano, none other than the two undercover officers who saved them from being killed in the Gonzales bust; Logan wants them to replace Ray and Danny as "the best of the worst."

During one of the attempts to capture Gonzales, Ray and Danny confiscate a large shipment of cocaine coming from [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia"). To get it back, Gonzales kidnaps Danny's ex-wife Anna, whom he still loves and has been trying to reconcile with, and says he will trade her for his drugs; otherwise, he will kill her. Danny agrees, leading to the final confrontation inside the high-rise atrium of the [State of Illinois Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_R._Thompson_Center "James R. Thompson Center"). During the ensuing fight, Danny and Ray rescue their would-be protégés in a way similar to their own rescuing, and Gonzales is killed. Anna and Danny reconcile and he and Ray decide not to retire after all.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Running_Scared_(1986_film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

In 2010, Hyams recalled that he had wanted "to remain earthbound" and desired a comedy that was "not stupid" and where the action was not "mean-spirited or bloody or graphic." MGM's script about retiring New York cops turned into a tale of non-retiring young Chicago cops, offering fresh casting possibilities and a unique city backdrop.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-globe-1) He noted that amidst numerous cop movies, he chose to opt for more unconventional actors and chose Billy Crystal and Gregory Hines, who proved to have great chemistry.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-peter-2)

Hines persistently campaigned for his role, proud that the film featured a "black guy [with] sex scenes," deviating from the norm of the black character being devoid of sexuality, as opposed to his white counterpart. He recalled that Hyams was "tough to work with" but that he didn't want to "put the guy down."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-hines-3) Crystal, valued for his improvisational skills, contributed "little pearls" to the script, supported by Hines' chemistry. He noted that his risky improvisations were only possible due to Hines' solid presence.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-billy-4)

Filming spanned September 1985 to January 1986 across MGM Studios in [Culver City, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culver_City,_California "Culver City, California"), in addition to location work in Key West, and Chicago.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-6)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Running_Scared_(1986_film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")]

_Running Scared_ was a moderate box office success, earning over $38 million. Reviews were mixed, however, and the film has a current 64% rating on [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), based on 25 reviews. The site's consensus states: "_Running Scared_ struggles to strike a consistent balance between violent action and humor, but the chemistry between its well-matched leads keeps things entertaining."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-7) Film critic [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") recommended it, saying that the film "transcends its dreary roots and turns out to be a lot of fun".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-8)

[Vincent Canby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Canby "Vincent Canby") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, however, advised people to "stay home and watch _[Miami Vice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami\_Vice "Miami Vice")_ or _[Cagney and Lacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cagney\_and\_Lacey "Cagney and Lacey")_" instead.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-9)

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Running_Scared_(1986_film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Box office")]

The film debuted at #5 at the U.S. box office, with a weekend gross of $5,227,757, with a total gross of $38.5 million.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-10) It was the 26th highest grossing movie of 1986.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-11)

_**Running Scared**_ is a 1986 American [buddy cop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_cop_film "Buddy cop film")[action comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_comedy_film "Action comedy film") shot and directed by [Peter Hyams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams "Peter Hyams"), and written by [Gary Devore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_DeVore_(screenwriter) "Gary DeVore (screenwriter)") and Jimmy Huston. It stars [Gregory Hines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregory_Hines "Gregory Hines") and [Billy Crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Crystal "Billy Crystal") as two Chicago police officers who attempt to bring down a drug dealer before they retire.

The film was released by [MGM Entertainment Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MGM_Entertainment_Co. "MGM Entertainment Co.") on June 27, 1986. It received mixed reviews, with praise for the performances of Hines and Crystal, but criticism for its mix of action and comedy, and grossed over $38 million.

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Running_Scared_(1986_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Ray Hughes and Danny Costanzo are two police officers working on Chicago's North Side, known for their wisecracking demeanors and unorthodox police methods, which get results in their various cases. One such case involves trying to bust up-and-coming drug dealer Julio Gonzales when they discovered he was released from prison. After arresting Snake, one of Gonzales's associates, they convince him to [wear a wire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiretapping "Wiretapping") in order to get the necessary evidence to put Gonzales away. When they approach the meeting place (a cargo ship) they find that Gonzales has acquired a large store of Israeli [Uzi submachine guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzi "Uzi"). Snake is setting the detectives up, however, prompting the detectives to rush in by acting as though Gonzales was preparing to kill him. Gonzales reveals his ambition to be the Spanish "[Godfather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vito_Corleone "Vito Corleone")" of Chicago, but chastises Snake for letting the detectives get close, and Snake is shot dead by a subordinate. The pair look as though they will be killed, but two undercover detectives in Gonzales's gang step in to make the arrest. In the ensuing gun battle, most of the gang escape, but Ray and Danny capture Gonzales.

Back at the station Ray and Danny expect to be praised, but instead their captain chastises them for their sloppy work (as revealed by Snake's wire) and orders them to take a vacation. On vacation in [Key West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_West "Key West"), the pair develop a fondness for the laid-back and enjoyable atmosphere, and begin to question their career choice after the experience; when they discuss life after being cops, they decide to retire and open a bar.

When they return to Chicago and inform the captain of their intentions, they find out that Gonzales has been released and is free on bail. Incensed, they vow to capture Gonzales before retiring, but by being a little more careful in the process, requisitioning bulletproof vests they never considered before. To add insult to injury, Captain Logan assigns them the additional task of training their replacements before they go. They must train detectives Anthony Montoya and Frank Sigliano, none other than the two undercover officers who saved them from being killed in the Gonzales bust; Logan wants them to replace Ray and Danny as "the best of the worst."

During one of the attempts to capture Gonzales, Ray and Danny confiscate a large shipment of cocaine coming from [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia"). To get it back, Gonzales kidnaps Danny's ex-wife Anna, whom he still loves and has been trying to reconcile with, and says he will trade her for his drugs; otherwise, he will kill her. Danny agrees, leading to the final confrontation inside the high-rise atrium of the [State of Illinois Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_R._Thompson_Center "James R. Thompson Center"). During the ensuing fight, Danny and Ray rescue their would-be protégés in a way similar to their own rescuing, and Gonzales is killed. Anna and Danny reconcile and he and Ray decide not to retire after all.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Running_Scared_(1986_film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

In 2010, Hyams recalled that he had wanted "to remain earthbound" and desired a comedy that was "not stupid" and where the action was not "mean-spirited or bloody or graphic." MGM's script about retiring New York cops turned into a tale of non-retiring young Chicago cops, offering fresh casting possibilities and a unique city backdrop.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-globe-1) He noted that amidst numerous cop movies, he chose to opt for more unconventional actors and chose Billy Crystal and Gregory Hines, who proved to have great chemistry.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-peter-2)

Hines persistently campaigned for his role, proud that the film featured a "black guy [with] sex scenes," deviating from the norm of the black character being devoid of sexuality, as opposed to his white counterpart. He recalled that Hyams was "tough to work with" but that he didn't want to "put the guy down."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-hines-3) Crystal, valued for his improvisational skills, contributed "little pearls" to the script, supported by Hines' chemistry. He noted that his risky improvisations were only possible due to Hines' solid presence.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-billy-4)

Filming spanned September 1985 to January 1986 across MGM Studios in [Culver City, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culver_City,_California "Culver City, California"), in addition to location work in Key West, and Chicago.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-6)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Running_Scared_(1986_film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")]

_Running Scared_ was a moderate box office success, earning over $38 million. Reviews were mixed, however, and the film has a current 64% rating on [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), based on 25 reviews. The site's consensus states: "_Running Scared_ struggles to strike a consistent balance between violent action and humor, but the chemistry between its well-matched leads keeps things entertaining."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-7) Film critic [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") recommended it, saying that the film "transcends its dreary roots and turns out to be a lot of fun".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-8)

[Vincent Canby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Canby "Vincent Canby") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, however, advised people to "stay home and watch _[Miami Vice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami\_Vice "Miami Vice")_ or _[Cagney and Lacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cagney\_and\_Lacey "Cagney and Lacey")_" instead.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-9)

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Running_Scared_(1986_film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Box office")]

The film debuted at #5 at the U.S. box office, with a weekend gross of $5,227,757, with a total gross of $38.5 million.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-10) It was the 26th highest grossing movie of 1986.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Scared_(1986_film)#cite_note-11)

**Syed Noor** is a famous [Pakistani](https://kids.kiddle.co/Pakistani "Pakistani")[film director](https://kids.kiddle.co/Movie_director "Movie director") who works in [Lahore](https://kids.kiddle.co/Lahore "Lahore"). He is also a producer, writer, and actor. His full name is Syed Ghulam Mohyuddin Noor. He is well-known for making many successful films in Pakistan.

## Contents

## Early Life and Learning

Syed Ghulam Mohyuddin Noor was born on February 21, 1950. His birthplace was [Lahore](https://kids.kiddle.co/Lahore "Lahore"), in [Punjab, Pakistan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Punjab_(Pakistan) "Punjab (Pakistan)"). He went to school in Lahore. Later, he earned a [Bachelor’s degree](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bachelor%27s_degree "Bachelor's degree") in [Journalism](https://kids.kiddle.co/Journalism "Journalism"). He studied at Government Dyal Singh College.

## His Film Career

Syed Noor started his journey in the film world in 1970. He first worked as an assistant to director S. Suleman. He helped S. Suleman make 18 movies. This experience taught him a lot about filmmaking.

### As a Writer

After helping as an assistant, Syed Noor wrote his first movie script. This was for the film _Society Girl_ in 1976. This movie was very popular and was considered one of the best films that year. Because of its success, Syed Noor became a top writer in the Pakistani film industry. He wrote for many famous directors.

From 1976 to 1992, Syed Noor wrote about 250 films. He wrote scripts in both Urdu and Punjabi languages. As a writer, he won many important awards. These included the National Award and the Nigar Award. People also offered him acting roles. However, he always wanted to direct movies. So, he turned down the acting offers.

### As a Director

In 1993, Syed Noor directed his first movie, _Qasam_. This film was a big hit at the box office. At that time, Punjabi films were very popular in Pakistan. Syed Noor wanted to bring back Urdu cinema. His next two films, _Jeeva_ (1995) and _Sargam_ (1995), helped him achieve this goal.

Syed Noor also helped many new actors start their careers. These actors later became very successful. As Urdu movies became popular again, Punjabi films started to be made less often. After the death of Punjabi film star [Sultan Rahi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Sultan_Rahi "Sultan Rahi"), Syed Noor decided to make Punjabi films again. His first Punjabi movie as a director was _Choorian_ (1998). This film was a huge success and is still one of the most popular Pakistani films ever. Another Punjabi film he directed, _Majajan_ (2006), also ran in cinemas for a very long time.

### Teaching Filmmaking

Syed Noor wanted to share his knowledge with new filmmakers. He started Paragon Studios and the Paragon Academy of Performing Arts. He also worked with the Mass Communications department at Punjab University. There, he began teaching film as a subject. Around this time, new movie theaters called multiplexes were built in Pakistan. Films also started to be made digitally. These changes gave new filmmakers many exciting chances to create movies.

## Awards and Honors

Syed Noor has written almost 300 films and directed 55 films. He has won more than 10 National Awards and many other honors. In 2013, the Pakistani government gave him a very special award. This was the "Sitara-i-Imtiaz" (Star of Excellence) Award. It is one of the highest awards a civilian can receive in Pakistan.

*   Sitara-i-Imtiaz (Star of Excellence) Award by the [President of Pakistan](https://kids.kiddle.co/President_of_Pakistan "President of Pakistan") in 2013
*   Nigar Award for Best Film Director in 1995, 1996, and 1997
