**Gulzar**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-1) (Urdu pronunciation:[[ɡʊlzɑːɾ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu"); born **Sampooran Singh Kalra**; 18 August 1934) is an Indian [Urdu poet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu_poetry "Urdu poetry"), [lyricist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyricist "Lyricist"), [author](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Author "Author"), [screenwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenwriter "Screenwriter"), and [film director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_director "Film director") known for his works in [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-a-2) He is regarded as an important [Urdu poet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu_poet "Urdu poet") of this era.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-3) He started his career with music director [S.D. Burman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.D._Burman "S.D. Burman") as a lyricist in the 1963 film _[Bandini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandini\_(film) "Bandini (film)")_ and worked with many music directors including [R. D. Burman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R._D._Burman "R. D. Burman"), [Salil Chowdhury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salil_Chowdhury "Salil Chowdhury"), [Vishal Bhardwaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal_Bhardwaj "Vishal Bhardwaj") and [A. R. Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._R._Rahman "A. R. Rahman").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-5) Gulzar also writes poetry, dialogues and scripts. He directed films such as _[Aandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aandhi "Aandhi")_ and _[Mausam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausam\_(1975\_film) "Mausam (1975 film)")_ during the 1970s and the TV series _[Mirza Ghalib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirza\_Ghalib\_(TV\_series) "Mirza Ghalib (TV series)")_ in the 1980s. He also directed _[Kirdaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirdaar "Kirdaar")_ in 1993.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-6) He attended United Christian School Ludlow Castle Delhi. He indicated this in Rekhta Prog in an interview by Divya Dutta.

Gulzar has won 5 Indian [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards"); including [2 Best Lyrics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Lyrics "National Film Award for Best Lyrics"), [one Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "National Film Award for Best Screenplay"), [one Second Best Feature Film (director)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Second_Best_Feature_Film "National Film Award for Second Best Feature Film"), and [one Best Popular Film (director)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Popular_Film_Providing_Wholesome_Entertainment "National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment"); 22 [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"); one [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award"); and one [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-IndiaToday-20140412-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8) He was awarded the [Sahitya Akademi Award - Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahitya_Akademi_Award "Sahitya Akademi Award") in 2002, the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") in 2004, the third-highest civilian award in India, and the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award") in 2013, the highest award in Indian cinema. In April 2013, Gulzar was appointed as the Chancellor of the Assam University.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Padma_Awards-9) In 2024, Gulzar was awarded the [Jnanpith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jnanpith_Award "Jnanpith Award"), India's highest literary award.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-10)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Gulzar was born in a [Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikhs "Sikhs") Khatri family as Sampooran Singh Kalra, to Makhan Singh Kalra and Sujan Kaur, in [Dina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dina,_Pakistan "Dina, Pakistan"), [Jhelum District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhelum_District "Jhelum District"), [British India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") (present-day [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan")). In school, he had read translations of the works of [Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagore "Tagore") which he recounted as one of his life's many turning points. Due to the [partition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India"), his family split and he had to stop his studies and come to [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") (then called Bombay) to support his family. Sampooran took up many small jobs in Mumbai to eke out a living, including one at a garage at _Vichare motors_ on Bellasis road ([Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai")).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-11) There he used to touch up accident-damaged cars by mixing shades of paint. He'd say, "I had a knack for colours". His father rebuked him for being a writer initially. He took the pen name **Gulzar Deenvi** and later simply **Gulzar**.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-meghna-12) In an interview with Rajyasabha TV, he recounted enjoying his work as a painter as it allowed him a lot of time to simultaneously read, write, attend college and be involved with the PWA (Progressive Writers Association).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-a-2)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-14)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Lyricist

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Lyricist")]

It was during his interactions in the PWA Sunday meetings that [Shailendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shailendra_(lyricist) "Shailendra (lyricist)") and [Bimal Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bimal_Roy "Bimal Roy") encouraged him to join films. Gulzar began his career under film directors [Bimal Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bimal_Roy "Bimal Roy") and [Hrishikesh Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrishikesh_Mukherjee "Hrishikesh Mukherjee"). His book _Ravi Paar_ has a narrative of Bimal Roy and the agony of creation. He started his career as a songwriter with the music director for the movie _[Bandini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandini\_(1963\_film) "Bandini (1963 film)")_ (1963). In films, he found an environment associated with literature in the group he worked with, including Bimal Roy, most of whose films were based on literary works.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Man-Of-many-seasons-15)[Shailendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shailendra_(lyricist) "Shailendra (lyricist)"), who has penned the rest of the songs in the movie requested Gulzar to write the song "Mora Gora Ang Layle", sung by [Lata Mangeshkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lata_Mangeshkar "Lata Mangeshkar").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-IndiaToday-20140412-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)

Directed and produced by [Hrishikesh Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrishikesh_Mukherjee "Hrishikesh Mukherjee"), the 1968 film _[Aashirwad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aashirwad\_(film) "Aashirwad (film)")_ had dialogues and lyrics written by Gulzar. Song lyrics and poems written by Gulzar gave the poetic attribute and the "much-needed additional dimension"[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Aashirwad-17) to [Ashok Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashok_Kumar "Ashok Kumar")'s role in the film. Ashok Kumar received the Best Actor [at the Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Actor") and [at the National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor") for this role.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Aashirwad-17) Gulzar's lyrics, however, did not gain much attention until 1969's _[Khamoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khamoshi\_(1970\_film) "Khamoshi (1970 film)")_, where his song "Humne Dekhi Hai Un Aankhon Ki Mehekti Khushboo" (lit.'I have seen the fragrance of those eyes') became popular. In his book _Bollywood Melodies, Ganesh Anantharaman_ describes Gulzar's lyrics, with the purposeful mixing of the senses, to be "daringly defiant".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-18)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-19)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-56thawardgiven-20) For the 1971 film _[Guddi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guddi\_(1971\_film) "Guddi (1971 film)")_, he penned two songs, of which "Humko Man Ki Shakti Dena" was a prayer which is still sung in many schools in India.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-21)

As a lyricist, Gulzar had a close association with the music director [Rahul Dev Burman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahul_Dev_Burman "Rahul Dev Burman"). He has also worked with [Sachin Dev Burman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sachin_Dev_Burman "Sachin Dev Burman"), [Shankar Jaikishan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar_Jaikishan "Shankar Jaikishan"), [Hemant Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemanta_Kumar_Mukhopadhyay "Hemanta Kumar Mukhopadhyay"), [Laxmikant–Pyarelal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxmikant%E2%80%93Pyarelal "Laxmikant–Pyarelal"), [Madan Mohan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madan_Mohan_(music_director) "Madan Mohan (music director)"), [Rajesh Roshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Roshan "Rajesh Roshan"), and [Anu Malik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anu_Malik "Anu Malik").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-IndiaToday-20140412-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-22) Gulzar worked with [Salil Chowdhury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salil_Chowdhury "Salil Chowdhury") in _[Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand\_(1971\_film) "Anand (1971 film)")_ (1971) and _[Mere Apne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mere\_Apne "Mere Apne")_ (1971); [Madan Mohan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madan_Mohan "Madan Mohan") in _[Mausam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausam\_(1975\_film) "Mausam (1975 film)")_ (1975), and more recently with [Vishal Bhardwaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal_Bhardwaj "Vishal Bhardwaj") in _[Maachis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maachis "Maachis")_ (1996), _[Omkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omkara\_(2006\_film) "Omkara (2006 film)")_ (2006) and _[Kaminey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaminey "Kaminey")_ (2009); [A. R. Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._R._Rahman "A. R. Rahman") in _[Dil Se..](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Se.. "Dil Se..")_ (1998), _[Guru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guru\_(2007\_film) "Guru (2007 film)")_ (2007), _[Slumdog Millionaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slumdog\_Millionaire "Slumdog Millionaire")_ (2008) and _[Raavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raavan\_(2010\_Hindi\_film) "Raavan (2010 Hindi film)")_ (2010) and [Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar%E2%80%93Ehsaan%E2%80%93Loy "Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy") in _[Bunty Aur Babli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunty\_Aur\_Babli "Bunty Aur Babli")_ (2005).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-IndiaToday-20140412-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16) Gulzar took inspiration from [Amir Khusrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amir_Khusrow "Amir Khusrow")'s "Ay Sarbathe Aashiqui" to pen "Ay Hairathe Aashiqui" for [Mani Ratnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mani_Ratnam "Mani Ratnam")'s 2007 Hindi film _[Guru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guru\_(soundtrack) "Guru (soundtrack)")_, which had music composed by [A. R. Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._R._Rahman "A. R. Rahman").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-23) Another Ratnam-Rahman hit, "[Chaiyya Chaiyya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaiyya_Chaiyya "Chaiyya Chaiyya")" from _Dil Se.._ also had lyrics written by Gulzar, based on the Sufi folk song "Thaiyya Thaiyya", with lyrics by poet [Bulleh Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulleh_Shah "Bulleh Shah").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-24) For another collaboration with Rahman for [Danny Boyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Boyle "Danny Boyle")'s 2007 Hollywood film _[Slumdog Millionaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slumdog\_Millionaire "Slumdog Millionaire")_, Rahman and Gulzar won the [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") for [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song") for "[Jai Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jai_Ho_(song) "Jai Ho (song)")" at the [81st Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Academy_Awards "81st Academy Awards"). The song received international acclaim and won him a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") (shared with Rahman) in the category of [Grammy Award for Best Song Written for a Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Song_Written_for_a_Motion_Picture,_Television_or_Other_Visual_Media "Grammy Award for Best Song Written for a Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-IndiaToday-20140412-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ffall-25)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-gk-26) He also wrote a song for the Pakistani Drama _[Shehryar Shehzadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shehryar\_Shehzadi "Shehryar Shehzadi")_, and this song _Teri Raza_, has been sung by [Rekha Bhardwaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rekha_Bhardwaj "Rekha Bhardwaj") and was composed by [Vishal Bhardwaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal_Bhardwaj "Vishal Bhardwaj").

### Direction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Direction")]

After writing dialogues and screenplay for films such as _Aashirwad_, _Anand_ and _Khamoshi_, Gulzar directed his first film _[Mere Apne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mere\_Apne "Mere Apne")_ (1971). The film was a remake of [Tapan Sinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapan_Sinha "Tapan Sinha")'s Bengali film _[Apanjan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apanjan "Apanjan")_ (1969). [Meena Kumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meena_Kumari "Meena Kumari") played the lead role of Anandi Devi, an old widow caught in between the local fights of unemployed and tormented youngsters. Anandi Devi's death in one of the fights makes them realise the futility of violence. The film was rated "Above Average" at the box office.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-27) He then directed _[Parichay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parichay\_(film) "Parichay (film)")_ and _[Koshish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koshish "Koshish")_. _Parichay_ was based on a Bengali novel, _Rangeen Uttarain_ by Raj Kumar Maitra and inspired from the Hollywood film _[The Sound of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sound\_of\_Music\_(film) "The Sound of Music (film)")_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-EHC_2003-28) He wrote the story of _Koshish_ based on the struggle faced by a deaf-dumb couple wherein [Sanjeev Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjeev_Kumar "Sanjeev Kumar") won [National Film Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-29) In 1973, he directed _[Achanak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achanak\_(1973\_film) "Achanak (1973 film)")_, inspired by the 1958 murder case [KM Nanavati v State of Maharashtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KM_Nanavati_v_State_of_Maharashtra "KM Nanavati v State of Maharashtra"), and the story writer [Khwaja Ahmad Abbas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khwaja_Ahmad_Abbas "Khwaja Ahmad Abbas") earned a [Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards") nomination for [Best Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Story "Filmfare Award for Best Story").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-30) Later he directed _[Aandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aandhi "Aandhi")_, based on the Hindi novel "Kaali Aandhi" by [Kamleshwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamleshwar_(writer) "Kamleshwar (writer)"). Along with various wins and nominations, the film also won [Filmfare Critics Award for Best Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Critics_Award_for_Best_Movie "Filmfare Critics Award for Best Movie"). Although many believed the film was based on the life of former Indian Prime Minister [Indira Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi "Indira Gandhi"), the film was actually based on the life of Bihari politician,[Tarkeshwari Sinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarkeshwari_Sinha "Tarkeshwari Sinha"). In the [1975's emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Emergency_(India) "The Emergency (India)"), the film was banned from theatres.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-EHC_2003-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Reality-31) His next film _[Khushboo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khushboo\_(1975\_film) "Khushboo (1975 film)")_ was based on [Sharat Chandra Chattopadhyay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharat_Chandra_Chattopadhyay "Sharat Chandra Chattopadhyay")'s _Pandit Mashay_. His _[Mausam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausam\_(1975\_film) "Mausam (1975 film)")_, which won the National Award for 2nd Best Feature Film,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-32)[Filmfare Best Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Best_Movie_Award "Filmfare Best Movie Award") and [Filmfare Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Best_Director_Award "Filmfare Best Director Award") awards, along with other six Filmfare nominations, was loosely based on the story _"Weather"_, from the novel, _[The Judas Tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Judas\_Tree "The Judas Tree")_, by [A.J. Cronin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.J._Cronin "A.J. Cronin"). His 1982 film _[Angoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angoor\_(1982\_film) "Angoor (1982 film)")_ was based on [Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakespeare "Shakespeare")'s play _[The Comedy of Errors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Comedy\_of\_Errors "The Comedy of Errors")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)

His films told stories of human relationships entangled in social issues. _[Libaas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libaas "Libaas")_ was a story of an extra-marital affair of an urban couple. Due to its objectionable subject, the film never got released in India.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-33)_Mausam_ pictured a story of a father who tries to improve the life of his prostitute-daughter. In _[Maachis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maachis "Maachis")_, a young Punjabi boy engages in terrorism to fight a bad situation only to realise its temporary nature. _[Hu Tu Tu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hu\_Tu\_Tu "Hu Tu Tu")_ dealt with corruption in India and how a man decides to fight it.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Hu_Tu_Tu_review-34)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Upperstall-35)

Gulzar uses "flashback" in the narration of his stories very effectively (_Aandhi, Mausam, Ijaazat, Machis, Hu Tu Tu_). He also has mutual partnerships with various actors and other crew. The Gulzar – [Sanjeev Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjeev_Kumar "Sanjeev Kumar") partnership resulted in some fine films (_Koshish, Aandhi, Mausam, Angoor, Namkeen_) which represent Sanjeev Kumar's finest work as an actor.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Upperstall-35) Actors like [Jeetendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeetendra "Jeetendra") (_Parichay, Khushboo, Kinara_), [Vinod Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinod_Khanna "Vinod Khanna") (_Achanak, Meera, Lekin_) and [Hema Malini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hema_Malini "Hema Malini") (_Khushboo, Kinara, Meera_) worked with Gulzar to gain respectability as artists and delivered some of their best and most introspective works in film.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Upperstall-35)[R D Burman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R_D_Burman "R D Burman") composed songs for almost all the movies directed by him in the 1970s and the 1980s (_Parichay, Khushboo, Aandhi, Angoor, Ijaazat, Libaas_). Many of their popular songs were sung by [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar"), [Lata Mangeshkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lata_Mangeshkar "Lata Mangeshkar") and [Asha Bhosle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asha_Bhosle "Asha Bhosle"). These include "Musafir Hoon Yaron" (_Parichay_), "Tere Bina Zindagi Se Koi" (_Aandhi_), and "[Mera Kuch Samaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mera_Kuch_Samaan "Mera Kuch Samaan")" (_Ijaazat_).[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Upperstall-35)

In 1988, Gulzar directed an [eponymous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eponym "Eponym") television serial _[Mirza Ghalib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirza\_Ghalib\_(TV\_series) "Mirza Ghalib (TV series)")_, starring [Naseeruddin Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeruddin_Shah "Naseeruddin Shah") and broadcast on [Doordarshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doordarshan "Doordarshan"). Later he also directed _Tahreer Munshi Premchand Ki_ about the novels of [Premchand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premchand "Premchand").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)

### Poetry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Poetry")]

Gulzar primarily writes in [Urdu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu "Urdu") and [Punjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_language "Punjabi language"); besides several other languages such as [Braj Bhasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braj_Bhasha "Braj Bhasha"), [Khariboli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kauravi_dialect "Kauravi dialect"), [Haryanvi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haryanvi_language "Haryanvi language") and [Marwari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marwari_language "Marwari language"). His poetry is in the [Triveni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triveni_(poetry) "Triveni (poetry)") type of stanza.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8) His poems are published in three compilations; _Chand Pukhraaj Ka_, _Raat Pashminey Ki_ and _Pandrah Paanch Pachattar_. His short stories are published in _Raavi-paar_ (also known as _Dustkhat_ in Pakistan) and _Dhuan_ (smoke).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)

For the peace campaign _[Aman ki Asha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aman\_ki\_Asha "Aman ki Asha")_, jointly started by India's and Pakistan's leading media houses, Gulzar wrote the anthem "Nazar Main Rehte Ho", which was recorded by [Shankar Mahadevan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar_Mahadevan "Shankar Mahadevan") and [Rahat Fateh Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahat_Fateh_Ali_Khan "Rahat Fateh Ali Khan").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-36) Gulzar has written ghazals for Ghazal Maestro [Jagjit Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jagjit_Singh "Jagjit Singh")'s albums "Marasim" (1999) and "Koi Baat Chale" (2006).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-37)

### Other contributions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Other contributions")]

Gulzar has written lyrics and dialogues for several [Doordarshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doordarshan "Doordarshan") TV series including _[Jungle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jungle\_Book\_Sh%C5%8Dnen\_Mowgli "Jungle Book Shōnen Mowgli")_, _[Alice in Wonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fushigi\_no\_Kuni\_no\_Alice "Fushigi no Kuni no Alice")_, _[Hello Zindagi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hello\_Zindagi "Hello Zindagi")_, _Guchche_ and _[Potli Baba Ki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potli\_Baba\_Ki "Potli Baba Ki")_ with [Vishal Bhardwaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal_Bhardwaj "Vishal Bhardwaj"). He has more recently written and narrated for the children's audiobook series _[Karadi Tales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karadi\_Tales "Karadi Tales")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-38) Gulzar is also associated with Aarushi,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-:0-39)[Eklavya foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eklavya_foundation "Eklavya foundation"), an NGO based in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh working in the field of education.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-:0-39)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-40)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-41) He has written stories and poetry for the magazine [Chakmak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chakmak "Chakmak"). Gulzar has also worked in Bollywood movies like [Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand_(1971_film) "Anand (1971 film)"), [Mere Apne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mere_Apne "Mere Apne"), [Omkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omkara_(2006_film) "Omkara (2006 film)") and many more.

### Academic

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Academic")]

In April 2013, Gulzar was appointed as the Chancellor of the [Assam University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assam_University "Assam University").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-42)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Gulzar is married to actress [Raakhee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raakhee "Raakhee"). The couple has a daughter, [Meghna Gulzar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meghna_Gulzar "Meghna Gulzar"). Meghna Gulzar grew up with her mother and father and, after completing her graduation in filmmaking from [New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University"), went on to become a director of films such as _[Filhaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filhaal "Filhaal")_, _[Just Married](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just\_Married\_(2007\_film) "Just Married (2007 film)")_, _[Dus Kahaniyaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dus\_Kahaniyaan "Dus Kahaniyaan")_, [Talvar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talvar_(film) "Talvar (film)"), _[Raazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raazi "Raazi")_, _[Sam Bahadur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam\_Bahadur\_(film) "Sam Bahadur (film)")_ and _[Chhapaak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chhapaak "Chhapaak")_[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-43) (for which Gulzar wrote the lyrics)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-44) and authored the biography of her father Gulzar, in 2004.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-45)

Gulzar received the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award") in 2013, presented by the President [Pranab Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pranab_Mukherjee "Pranab Mukherjee") at the [61st National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/61st_National_Film_Awards "61st National Film Awards")

As on 2019, Gulzar has won a total of 36 awards and honours, including 5 [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards"), 22 [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"), Rashtriya Kishore Kumar Samman from the Government of Madhya Pradesh for 1999–2000,[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-46)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-47) 1 [Academy Award for Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song") (2008), 1 [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") (2010), [2002 Sahitya Akademi Award for Urdu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Sahitya_Akademi_Award_winners_for_Urdu "List of Sahitya Akademi Award winners for Urdu"), [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") (2004), and 2013 [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award").

He received the [Jnanpith Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jnanpith_Award "Jnanpith Award") in 2024.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-48)

**Gulzar**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-1) (Urdu pronunciation:[[ɡʊlzɑːɾ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu"); born **Sampooran Singh Kalra**; 18 August 1934) is an Indian [Urdu poet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu_poetry "Urdu poetry"), [lyricist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyricist "Lyricist"), [author](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Author "Author"), [screenwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenwriter "Screenwriter"), and [film director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_director "Film director") known for his works in [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-a-2) He is regarded as an important [Urdu poet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu_poet "Urdu poet") of this era.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-3) He started his career with music director [S.D. Burman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.D._Burman "S.D. Burman") as a lyricist in the 1963 film _[Bandini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandini\_(film) "Bandini (film)")_ and worked with many music directors including [R. D. Burman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R._D._Burman "R. D. Burman"), [Salil Chowdhury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salil_Chowdhury "Salil Chowdhury"), [Vishal Bhardwaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal_Bhardwaj "Vishal Bhardwaj") and [A. R. Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._R._Rahman "A. R. Rahman").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-5) Gulzar also writes poetry, dialogues and scripts. He directed films such as _[Aandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aandhi "Aandhi")_ and _[Mausam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausam\_(1975\_film) "Mausam (1975 film)")_ during the 1970s and the TV series _[Mirza Ghalib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirza\_Ghalib\_(TV\_series) "Mirza Ghalib (TV series)")_ in the 1980s. He also directed _[Kirdaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirdaar "Kirdaar")_ in 1993.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-6) He attended United Christian School Ludlow Castle Delhi. He indicated this in Rekhta Prog in an interview by Divya Dutta.

Gulzar has won 5 Indian [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards"); including [2 Best Lyrics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Lyrics "National Film Award for Best Lyrics"), [one Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "National Film Award for Best Screenplay"), [one Second Best Feature Film (director)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Second_Best_Feature_Film "National Film Award for Second Best Feature Film"), and [one Best Popular Film (director)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Popular_Film_Providing_Wholesome_Entertainment "National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment"); 22 [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"); one [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award"); and one [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-IndiaToday-20140412-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8) He was awarded the [Sahitya Akademi Award - Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahitya_Akademi_Award "Sahitya Akademi Award") in 2002, the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") in 2004, the third-highest civilian award in India, and the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award") in 2013, the highest award in Indian cinema. In April 2013, Gulzar was appointed as the Chancellor of the Assam University.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Padma_Awards-9) In 2024, Gulzar was awarded the [Jnanpith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jnanpith_Award "Jnanpith Award"), India's highest literary award.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-10)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Gulzar was born in a [Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikhs "Sikhs") Khatri family as Sampooran Singh Kalra, to Makhan Singh Kalra and Sujan Kaur, in [Dina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dina,_Pakistan "Dina, Pakistan"), [Jhelum District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhelum_District "Jhelum District"), [British India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") (present-day [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan")). In school, he had read translations of the works of [Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagore "Tagore") which he recounted as one of his life's many turning points. Due to the [partition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India"), his family split and he had to stop his studies and come to [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") (then called Bombay) to support his family. Sampooran took up many small jobs in Mumbai to eke out a living, including one at a garage at _Vichare motors_ on Bellasis road ([Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai")).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-11) There he used to touch up accident-damaged cars by mixing shades of paint. He'd say, "I had a knack for colours". His father rebuked him for being a writer initially. He took the pen name **Gulzar Deenvi** and later simply **Gulzar**.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-meghna-12) In an interview with Rajyasabha TV, he recounted enjoying his work as a painter as it allowed him a lot of time to simultaneously read, write, attend college and be involved with the PWA (Progressive Writers Association).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-a-2)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-14)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Lyricist

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Lyricist")]

It was during his interactions in the PWA Sunday meetings that [Shailendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shailendra_(lyricist) "Shailendra (lyricist)") and [Bimal Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bimal_Roy "Bimal Roy") encouraged him to join films. Gulzar began his career under film directors [Bimal Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bimal_Roy "Bimal Roy") and [Hrishikesh Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrishikesh_Mukherjee "Hrishikesh Mukherjee"). His book _Ravi Paar_ has a narrative of Bimal Roy and the agony of creation. He started his career as a songwriter with the music director for the movie _[Bandini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandini\_(1963\_film) "Bandini (1963 film)")_ (1963). In films, he found an environment associated with literature in the group he worked with, including Bimal Roy, most of whose films were based on literary works.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Man-Of-many-seasons-15)[Shailendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shailendra_(lyricist) "Shailendra (lyricist)"), who has penned the rest of the songs in the movie requested Gulzar to write the song "Mora Gora Ang Layle", sung by [Lata Mangeshkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lata_Mangeshkar "Lata Mangeshkar").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-IndiaToday-20140412-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)

Directed and produced by [Hrishikesh Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrishikesh_Mukherjee "Hrishikesh Mukherjee"), the 1968 film _[Aashirwad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aashirwad\_(film) "Aashirwad (film)")_ had dialogues and lyrics written by Gulzar. Song lyrics and poems written by Gulzar gave the poetic attribute and the "much-needed additional dimension"[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Aashirwad-17) to [Ashok Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashok_Kumar "Ashok Kumar")'s role in the film. Ashok Kumar received the Best Actor [at the Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Actor") and [at the National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor") for this role.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Aashirwad-17) Gulzar's lyrics, however, did not gain much attention until 1969's _[Khamoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khamoshi\_(1970\_film) "Khamoshi (1970 film)")_, where his song "Humne Dekhi Hai Un Aankhon Ki Mehekti Khushboo" (lit.'I have seen the fragrance of those eyes') became popular. In his book _Bollywood Melodies, Ganesh Anantharaman_ describes Gulzar's lyrics, with the purposeful mixing of the senses, to be "daringly defiant".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-18)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-19)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-56thawardgiven-20) For the 1971 film _[Guddi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guddi\_(1971\_film) "Guddi (1971 film)")_, he penned two songs, of which "Humko Man Ki Shakti Dena" was a prayer which is still sung in many schools in India.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-21)

As a lyricist, Gulzar had a close association with the music director [Rahul Dev Burman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahul_Dev_Burman "Rahul Dev Burman"). He has also worked with [Sachin Dev Burman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sachin_Dev_Burman "Sachin Dev Burman"), [Shankar Jaikishan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar_Jaikishan "Shankar Jaikishan"), [Hemant Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemanta_Kumar_Mukhopadhyay "Hemanta Kumar Mukhopadhyay"), [Laxmikant–Pyarelal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxmikant%E2%80%93Pyarelal "Laxmikant–Pyarelal"), [Madan Mohan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madan_Mohan_(music_director) "Madan Mohan (music director)"), [Rajesh Roshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Roshan "Rajesh Roshan"), and [Anu Malik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anu_Malik "Anu Malik").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-IndiaToday-20140412-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-22) Gulzar worked with [Salil Chowdhury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salil_Chowdhury "Salil Chowdhury") in _[Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand\_(1971\_film) "Anand (1971 film)")_ (1971) and _[Mere Apne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mere\_Apne "Mere Apne")_ (1971); [Madan Mohan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madan_Mohan "Madan Mohan") in _[Mausam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausam\_(1975\_film) "Mausam (1975 film)")_ (1975), and more recently with [Vishal Bhardwaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal_Bhardwaj "Vishal Bhardwaj") in _[Maachis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maachis "Maachis")_ (1996), _[Omkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omkara\_(2006\_film) "Omkara (2006 film)")_ (2006) and _[Kaminey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaminey "Kaminey")_ (2009); [A. R. Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._R._Rahman "A. R. Rahman") in _[Dil Se..](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Se.. "Dil Se..")_ (1998), _[Guru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guru\_(2007\_film) "Guru (2007 film)")_ (2007), _[Slumdog Millionaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slumdog\_Millionaire "Slumdog Millionaire")_ (2008) and _[Raavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raavan\_(2010\_Hindi\_film) "Raavan (2010 Hindi film)")_ (2010) and [Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar%E2%80%93Ehsaan%E2%80%93Loy "Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy") in _[Bunty Aur Babli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunty\_Aur\_Babli "Bunty Aur Babli")_ (2005).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-IndiaToday-20140412-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16) Gulzar took inspiration from [Amir Khusrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amir_Khusrow "Amir Khusrow")'s "Ay Sarbathe Aashiqui" to pen "Ay Hairathe Aashiqui" for [Mani Ratnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mani_Ratnam "Mani Ratnam")'s 2007 Hindi film _[Guru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guru\_(soundtrack) "Guru (soundtrack)")_, which had music composed by [A. R. Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._R._Rahman "A. R. Rahman").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-23) Another Ratnam-Rahman hit, "[Chaiyya Chaiyya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaiyya_Chaiyya "Chaiyya Chaiyya")" from _Dil Se.._ also had lyrics written by Gulzar, based on the Sufi folk song "Thaiyya Thaiyya", with lyrics by poet [Bulleh Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulleh_Shah "Bulleh Shah").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-24) For another collaboration with Rahman for [Danny Boyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Boyle "Danny Boyle")'s 2007 Hollywood film _[Slumdog Millionaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slumdog\_Millionaire "Slumdog Millionaire")_, Rahman and Gulzar won the [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") for [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song") for "[Jai Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jai_Ho_(song) "Jai Ho (song)")" at the [81st Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Academy_Awards "81st Academy Awards"). The song received international acclaim and won him a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") (shared with Rahman) in the category of [Grammy Award for Best Song Written for a Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Song_Written_for_a_Motion_Picture,_Television_or_Other_Visual_Media "Grammy Award for Best Song Written for a Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-IndiaToday-20140412-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ffall-25)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-gk-26) He also wrote a song for the Pakistani Drama _[Shehryar Shehzadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shehryar\_Shehzadi "Shehryar Shehzadi")_, and this song _Teri Raza_, has been sung by [Rekha Bhardwaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rekha_Bhardwaj "Rekha Bhardwaj") and was composed by [Vishal Bhardwaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal_Bhardwaj "Vishal Bhardwaj").

### Direction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Direction")]

After writing dialogues and screenplay for films such as _Aashirwad_, _Anand_ and _Khamoshi_, Gulzar directed his first film _[Mere Apne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mere\_Apne "Mere Apne")_ (1971). The film was a remake of [Tapan Sinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapan_Sinha "Tapan Sinha")'s Bengali film _[Apanjan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apanjan "Apanjan")_ (1969). [Meena Kumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meena_Kumari "Meena Kumari") played the lead role of Anandi Devi, an old widow caught in between the local fights of unemployed and tormented youngsters. Anandi Devi's death in one of the fights makes them realise the futility of violence. The film was rated "Above Average" at the box office.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-27) He then directed _[Parichay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parichay\_(film) "Parichay (film)")_ and _[Koshish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koshish "Koshish")_. _Parichay_ was based on a Bengali novel, _Rangeen Uttarain_ by Raj Kumar Maitra and inspired from the Hollywood film _[The Sound of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sound\_of\_Music\_(film) "The Sound of Music (film)")_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-EHC_2003-28) He wrote the story of _Koshish_ based on the struggle faced by a deaf-dumb couple wherein [Sanjeev Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjeev_Kumar "Sanjeev Kumar") won [National Film Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-29) In 1973, he directed _[Achanak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achanak\_(1973\_film) "Achanak (1973 film)")_, inspired by the 1958 murder case [KM Nanavati v State of Maharashtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KM_Nanavati_v_State_of_Maharashtra "KM Nanavati v State of Maharashtra"), and the story writer [Khwaja Ahmad Abbas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khwaja_Ahmad_Abbas "Khwaja Ahmad Abbas") earned a [Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards") nomination for [Best Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Story "Filmfare Award for Best Story").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-30) Later he directed _[Aandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aandhi "Aandhi")_, based on the Hindi novel "Kaali Aandhi" by [Kamleshwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamleshwar_(writer) "Kamleshwar (writer)"). Along with various wins and nominations, the film also won [Filmfare Critics Award for Best Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Critics_Award_for_Best_Movie "Filmfare Critics Award for Best Movie"). Although many believed the film was based on the life of former Indian Prime Minister [Indira Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi "Indira Gandhi"), the film was actually based on the life of Bihari politician,[Tarkeshwari Sinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarkeshwari_Sinha "Tarkeshwari Sinha"). In the [1975's emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Emergency_(India) "The Emergency (India)"), the film was banned from theatres.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-EHC_2003-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Reality-31) His next film _[Khushboo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khushboo\_(1975\_film) "Khushboo (1975 film)")_ was based on [Sharat Chandra Chattopadhyay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharat_Chandra_Chattopadhyay "Sharat Chandra Chattopadhyay")'s _Pandit Mashay_. His _[Mausam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausam\_(1975\_film) "Mausam (1975 film)")_, which won the National Award for 2nd Best Feature Film,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-32)[Filmfare Best Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Best_Movie_Award "Filmfare Best Movie Award") and [Filmfare Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Best_Director_Award "Filmfare Best Director Award") awards, along with other six Filmfare nominations, was loosely based on the story _"Weather"_, from the novel, _[The Judas Tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Judas\_Tree "The Judas Tree")_, by [A.J. Cronin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.J._Cronin "A.J. Cronin"). His 1982 film _[Angoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angoor\_(1982\_film) "Angoor (1982 film)")_ was based on [Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakespeare "Shakespeare")'s play _[The Comedy of Errors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Comedy\_of\_Errors "The Comedy of Errors")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)

His films told stories of human relationships entangled in social issues. _[Libaas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libaas "Libaas")_ was a story of an extra-marital affair of an urban couple. Due to its objectionable subject, the film never got released in India.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-33)_Mausam_ pictured a story of a father who tries to improve the life of his prostitute-daughter. In _[Maachis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maachis "Maachis")_, a young Punjabi boy engages in terrorism to fight a bad situation only to realise its temporary nature. _[Hu Tu Tu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hu\_Tu\_Tu "Hu Tu Tu")_ dealt with corruption in India and how a man decides to fight it.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-toik-16)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Hu_Tu_Tu_review-34)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Upperstall-35)

Gulzar uses "flashback" in the narration of his stories very effectively (_Aandhi, Mausam, Ijaazat, Machis, Hu Tu Tu_). He also has mutual partnerships with various actors and other crew. The Gulzar – [Sanjeev Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjeev_Kumar "Sanjeev Kumar") partnership resulted in some fine films (_Koshish, Aandhi, Mausam, Angoor, Namkeen_) which represent Sanjeev Kumar's finest work as an actor.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Upperstall-35) Actors like [Jeetendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeetendra "Jeetendra") (_Parichay, Khushboo, Kinara_), [Vinod Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinod_Khanna "Vinod Khanna") (_Achanak, Meera, Lekin_) and [Hema Malini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hema_Malini "Hema Malini") (_Khushboo, Kinara, Meera_) worked with Gulzar to gain respectability as artists and delivered some of their best and most introspective works in film.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Upperstall-35)[R D Burman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R_D_Burman "R D Burman") composed songs for almost all the movies directed by him in the 1970s and the 1980s (_Parichay, Khushboo, Aandhi, Angoor, Ijaazat, Libaas_). Many of their popular songs were sung by [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar"), [Lata Mangeshkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lata_Mangeshkar "Lata Mangeshkar") and [Asha Bhosle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asha_Bhosle "Asha Bhosle"). These include "Musafir Hoon Yaron" (_Parichay_), "Tere Bina Zindagi Se Koi" (_Aandhi_), and "[Mera Kuch Samaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mera_Kuch_Samaan "Mera Kuch Samaan")" (_Ijaazat_).[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-Upperstall-35)

In 1988, Gulzar directed an [eponymous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eponym "Eponym") television serial _[Mirza Ghalib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirza\_Ghalib\_(TV\_series) "Mirza Ghalib (TV series)")_, starring [Naseeruddin Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeruddin_Shah "Naseeruddin Shah") and broadcast on [Doordarshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doordarshan "Doordarshan"). Later he also directed _Tahreer Munshi Premchand Ki_ about the novels of [Premchand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premchand "Premchand").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)

### Poetry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Poetry")]

Gulzar primarily writes in [Urdu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu "Urdu") and [Punjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_language "Punjabi language"); besides several other languages such as [Braj Bhasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braj_Bhasha "Braj Bhasha"), [Khariboli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kauravi_dialect "Kauravi dialect"), [Haryanvi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haryanvi_language "Haryanvi language") and [Marwari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marwari_language "Marwari language"). His poetry is in the [Triveni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triveni_(poetry) "Triveni (poetry)") type of stanza.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8) His poems are published in three compilations; _Chand Pukhraaj Ka_, _Raat Pashminey Ki_ and _Pandrah Paanch Pachattar_. His short stories are published in _Raavi-paar_ (also known as _Dustkhat_ in Pakistan) and _Dhuan_ (smoke).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)

For the peace campaign _[Aman ki Asha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aman\_ki\_Asha "Aman ki Asha")_, jointly started by India's and Pakistan's leading media houses, Gulzar wrote the anthem "Nazar Main Rehte Ho", which was recorded by [Shankar Mahadevan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar_Mahadevan "Shankar Mahadevan") and [Rahat Fateh Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahat_Fateh_Ali_Khan "Rahat Fateh Ali Khan").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-36) Gulzar has written ghazals for Ghazal Maestro [Jagjit Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jagjit_Singh "Jagjit Singh")'s albums "Marasim" (1999) and "Koi Baat Chale" (2006).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-37)

### Other contributions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Other contributions")]

Gulzar has written lyrics and dialogues for several [Doordarshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doordarshan "Doordarshan") TV series including _[Jungle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jungle\_Book\_Sh%C5%8Dnen\_Mowgli "Jungle Book Shōnen Mowgli")_, _[Alice in Wonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fushigi\_no\_Kuni\_no\_Alice "Fushigi no Kuni no Alice")_, _[Hello Zindagi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hello\_Zindagi "Hello Zindagi")_, _Guchche_ and _[Potli Baba Ki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potli\_Baba\_Ki "Potli Baba Ki")_ with [Vishal Bhardwaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal_Bhardwaj "Vishal Bhardwaj"). He has more recently written and narrated for the children's audiobook series _[Karadi Tales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karadi\_Tales "Karadi Tales")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-ix-8)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-38) Gulzar is also associated with Aarushi,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-:0-39)[Eklavya foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eklavya_foundation "Eklavya foundation"), an NGO based in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh working in the field of education.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-:0-39)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-40)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-41) He has written stories and poetry for the magazine [Chakmak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chakmak "Chakmak"). Gulzar has also worked in Bollywood movies like [Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand_(1971_film) "Anand (1971 film)"), [Mere Apne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mere_Apne "Mere Apne"), [Omkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omkara_(2006_film) "Omkara (2006 film)") and many more.

### Academic

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Academic")]

In April 2013, Gulzar was appointed as the Chancellor of the [Assam University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assam_University "Assam University").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-42)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gulzar&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Gulzar is married to actress [Raakhee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raakhee "Raakhee"). The couple has a daughter, [Meghna Gulzar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meghna_Gulzar "Meghna Gulzar"). Meghna Gulzar grew up with her mother and father and, after completing her graduation in filmmaking from [New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University"), went on to become a director of films such as _[Filhaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filhaal "Filhaal")_, _[Just Married](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just\_Married\_(2007\_film) "Just Married (2007 film)")_, _[Dus Kahaniyaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dus\_Kahaniyaan "Dus Kahaniyaan")_, [Talvar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talvar_(film) "Talvar (film)"), _[Raazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raazi "Raazi")_, _[Sam Bahadur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam\_Bahadur\_(film) "Sam Bahadur (film)")_ and _[Chhapaak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chhapaak "Chhapaak")_[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-43) (for which Gulzar wrote the lyrics)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-44) and authored the biography of her father Gulzar, in 2004.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-45)

Gulzar received the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award") in 2013, presented by the President [Pranab Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pranab_Mukherjee "Pranab Mukherjee") at the [61st National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/61st_National_Film_Awards "61st National Film Awards")

As on 2019, Gulzar has won a total of 36 awards and honours, including 5 [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards"), 22 [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"), Rashtriya Kishore Kumar Samman from the Government of Madhya Pradesh for 1999–2000,[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-46)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-47) 1 [Academy Award for Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song") (2008), 1 [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") (2010), [2002 Sahitya Akademi Award for Urdu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Sahitya_Akademi_Award_winners_for_Urdu "List of Sahitya Akademi Award winners for Urdu"), [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") (2004), and 2013 [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award").

He received the [Jnanpith Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jnanpith_Award "Jnanpith Award") in 2024.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar#cite_note-48)

Michael Radford was born on 24 February 1946 in New Delhi, British India [now India]. He is a director and writer, known for [1984 (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087803/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [The Postman (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0110877/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [The Merchant of Venice (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0379889/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He is married to [Emma Tweed](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1912817/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). They have two children. He was previously married to Iseult Teran.

Michael Radford was born on 24 February 1946 in New Delhi, British India [now India]. He is a director and writer, known for [1984 (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087803/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [The Postman (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0110877/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [The Merchant of Venice (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0379889/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He is married to [Emma Tweed](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1912817/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). They have two children. He was previously married to Iseult Teran.

**Peter Hyams** (born July 26, 1943) is an American [film director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_director "Film director"), [screenwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenwriter "Screenwriter") and [cinematographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematographer "Cinematographer") known for directing the 1977 conspiracy thriller film _[Capricorn One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capricorn\_One "Capricorn One")_ (which he also wrote), the 1981 science fiction-thriller _[Outland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outland\_(film) "Outland (film)")_, the 1984 science fiction film _[2010: The Year We Make Contact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010:\_The\_Year\_We\_Make\_Contact "2010: The Year We Make Contact")_ (a sequel to [Stanley Kubrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Kubrick "Stanley Kubrick")'s _[2001: A Space Odyssey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001:\_A\_Space\_Odyssey\_(film) "2001: A Space Odyssey (film)")_), the 1986 action/comedy _[Running Scared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running\_Scared\_(1986\_film) "Running Scared (1986 film)")_, the comic book adaptation _[Timecop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timecop "Timecop")_, the action film _[Sudden Death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudden\_Death\_(1995\_film) "Sudden Death (1995 film)")_ (both starring [Jean-Claude Van Damme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Claude_Van_Damme "Jean-Claude Van Damme")), and the horror films _[The Relic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Relic "The Relic")_ and _[End of Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End\_of\_Days\_(film) "End of Days (film)")_.

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Hyams&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

### Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Hyams&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early life")]

Hyams was born in New York City, New York, the son of Ruth Hurok and Barry Hyams, who was a [theatrical producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_producer "Theatrical producer") and publicist on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre"). His maternal grandfather was [Sol Hurok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sol_Hurok "Sol Hurok"), the Russian [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jew "Jew")[impresario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impresario "Impresario"). His stepfather was [blacklisted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blacklist "Blacklist") conductor Arthur Lief. His sister was [casting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casting_(performing_arts) "Casting (performing arts)") director [Nessa Hyams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nessa_Hyams "Nessa Hyams").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-lukeford-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-2) His son, [John Hyams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hyams "John Hyams"), is also a film director.

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Hyams&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Television")]

Hyams studied art and music at [Hunter College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter_College "Hunter College") and [Syracuse University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_University "Syracuse University") before working as a producer/[anchorman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchorman "Anchorman") for [WHDH-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WHDH-TV_(defunct) "WHDH-TV (defunct)"). During 1966 while working for a CBS owned station in New York, he served three months as a news correspondent in Vietnam. He worked in Boston then in January 1968 he joined [WBBM-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WBBM-TV "WBBM-TV") in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago") as an anchorman and reporter to replace [Fahey Flynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fahey_Flynn "Fahey Flynn").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-3) A contemporary report described him as a "glamor type".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-4)

During his time with CBS (where he worked from 1964 to 1970), he then began to shoot [documentary films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Documentary_film "Documentary film").

### Screenwriter

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Hyams&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Screenwriter")]

Hyams moved to Los Angeles in 1970 where he sold his first screenplay, _[T.R. Baskin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T.R.\_Baskin "T.R. Baskin")_, to [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures") in 1971. [Herbert Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Ross "Herbert Ross") directed the film and Hyams produced.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-lukeford-1)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-6)

### Directing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Hyams&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Directing")]

Hyams made his directorial debut with an [ABC Movie of the Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Movie_of_the_Week "ABC Movie of the Week") for [Aaron Spelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Spelling "Aaron Spelling"), _[Rolling Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Man "Rolling Man")_ (1972) starring [Dennis Weaver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Weaver "Dennis Weaver"). Hyams worked on it solely as director, with the script being written by the producers.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-7)

Hyams followed it directing another TV movie which he also wrote, _[Goodnight, My Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodnight,\_My\_Love "Goodnight, My Love")_ (1972), about a private eye and a dwarf. The film was highly acclaimed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-8)

Hyams optioned a novel _Going All the Way_ which he intended to adapt and direct but it was not made.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-9)

The praise for _Goodnight My Love_ meant Hyams was able to get finance for his debut feature as writer-director, _[Busting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busting "Busting")_ (1974), a buddy cop movie starring [Elliott Gould](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliott_Gould "Elliott Gould") and Robert Blake. He followed it with _[Our Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our\_Time\_(1974\_film) "Our Time (1974 film)")_ (1974), a romance with [Pamela Sue Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Sue_Martin "Pamela Sue Martin"), which he directed only.

Hyams made _[Peeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peeper\_(film) "Peeper (film)")_ (1975), for the producers of _Busting_ with [Michael Caine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Caine "Michael Caine") and [Natalie Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natalie_Wood "Natalie Wood"). It was a financial failure and Hyams' career was at a low ebb. He wrote the script _Hanover Street_ which he could have sold outright but Hyams insisted on directing. He wrote the screenplay for the Charles Bronson thriller _[Telefon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telefon\_(film) "Telefon (film)")_ (1977), doing a draft for [Richard Lester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Lester "Richard Lester") (who ended up not directing the film). It was rewritten extensively.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-money-10)

### _Capricorn One_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Hyams&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Capricorn One")]

Hyams had written the script for _[Capricorn One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capricorn\_One "Capricorn One")_ (1977) a number of years earlier. It was a conspiracy thriller about a faked mission to Mars. Paul Lazarus managed to raise financing with Hyams as director and the film was his first hit.

This was followed by the less successful _[Hanover Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanover\_Street\_(film) "Hanover Street (film)")_ (1979), which starred [Harrison Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford "Harrison Ford").

Hyams did a rewrite of [Ted Leighton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levinson_&_Link "Levinson & Link")'s screenplay for the [Steve McQueen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_McQueen "Steve McQueen") film _[The Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hunter\_(1980\_film) "The Hunter (1980 film)")_ (1980) which he was to direct. However, he dropped out after clashes with McQueen.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-11)

He wanted to do a Western but was unable to get financing, so he then wrote and directed the science fiction cult classic _[Outland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outland\_(film) "Outland (film)")_ (1981), which starred [Sean Connery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Connery "Sean Connery") in a 'High Noon' scenario set on [Io](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Io_(moon) "Io (moon)"), one of Jupiter's moons.

Hyams directed the thriller _[The Star Chamber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Star\_Chamber\_(film) "The Star Chamber (film)")_ (1983), starring [Michael Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Douglas "Michael Douglas"), also rewriting the script.

### MGM

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Hyams&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: MGM")]

For MGM Hyams produced, directed, and wrote the screenplay for _[2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010\_(film) "2010 (film)")_ (1984), collaborating closely with author [Arthur C. Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_C._Clarke "Arthur C. Clarke") (_[2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010:\_Odyssey\_Two "2010: Odyssey Two")_).

Hyams also co-authored with Clarke _The Odyssey File: The Making of 2010_, published 1985, a collection of their [email](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Email "Email") correspondence which illustrates their fascination with the then pioneering medium, and its use for them to communicate on an almost daily basis while planning and producing the film.

Hyams directed an episode of _[Amazing Stories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazing\_Stories\_(1985\_TV\_series) "Amazing Stories (1985 TV series)")_, "The Amazing Falsworth".

Hyams had a hit with a buddy cop film, _[Running Scared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running\_Scared\_(1986\_film) "Running Scared (1986 film)")_ (1986) at MGM with [Gregory Hines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregory_Hines "Gregory Hines") and [Billy Crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Crystal "Billy Crystal").

He followed it with _[The Presidio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Presidio\_(film) "The Presidio (film)")_ (1988), another buddy action film, starring [Sean Connery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Connery "Sean Connery") and [Mark Harmon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Harmon "Mark Harmon"). In between he executive produced the 1980s cult kids movie _[The Monster Squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Monster\_Squad "The Monster Squad")_ (1987).

Less popular was _[Narrow Margin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narrow\_Margin\_(1990\_film) "Narrow Margin (1990 film)")_ (1990), a remake of the 1952 film, and the comedy _[Stay Tuned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stay\_Tuned\_(film) "Stay Tuned (film)")_ (1992).

### Jean-Claude Van Damme

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Hyams&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Jean-Claude Van Damme")]

Hyams had a big hit with the [Jean-Claude Van Damme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Claude_Van_Damme "Jean-Claude Van Damme") film _[Timecop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timecop "Timecop")_ (1994). The director and actor subsequently reteamed on _[Sudden Death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudden\_Death\_(1995\_film) "Sudden Death (1995 film)")_ (1995) which did less well.

Hyams did a horror monster movie called _[The Relic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Relic "The Relic")_ (1997) which received mixed reviews and grossed $48 million at the box office.

The blockbuster _[End of Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End\_of\_Days\_(film) "End of Days (film)")_ (1999) starring [Arnold Schwarzenegger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_Schwarzenegger "Arnold Schwarzenegger") is the highest-grossing film in Hyams' career, grossing over $200 million at the worldwide box-office but was met with negative critical reception.

Hyams followed with _[The Musketeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Musketeer "The Musketeer")_ (2001), a new version of the novel by [Alexandre Dumas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandre_Dumas "Alexandre Dumas"), which was a minor box office success.

However, his next film, _[A Sound of Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Sound\_of\_Thunder\_(film) "A Sound of Thunder (film)")_ (2005), a science-fiction movie, had serious difficulties during its production (including the bankruptcy of the original production company during post-production), performed particularly badly at the box office worldwide and was poorly received by critics.

He directed an episode of the series _[Threshold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threshold\_(TV\_series) "Threshold (TV series)")_ (2005).

In 2007, it was reported that he would direct the remake of his own _[Capricorn One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capricorn\_One "Capricorn One")_;[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-filmjunk-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-13) instead, he directed the remake of the [1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_in_film "1956 in film")[film noir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_noir "Film noir")_[Beyond a Reasonable Doubt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyond\_a\_Reasonable\_Doubt\_(1956\_film) "Beyond a Reasonable Doubt (1956 film)")_ starring [Michael Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Douglas "Michael Douglas"), which was released in 2009. It was a [box office flop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box-office_bomb "Box-office bomb"), and panned by critics.

### Reunion with Van Damme

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Hyams&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Reunion with Van Damme")]

Hyams also contributed the cinematography to his son John's effort, _[Universal Soldier: Regeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal\_Soldier:\_Regeneration "Universal Soldier: Regeneration")_, the third official _[Universal Soldier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal\_Soldier\_(series) "Universal Soldier (series)")_ sequel starring [Jean-Claude Van Damme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Claude_Van_Damme "Jean-Claude Van Damme") and [Dolph Lundgren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolph_Lundgren "Dolph Lundgren").

Hyams directed the thriller _[Enemies Closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enemies\_Closer "Enemies Closer")_ which began filming in late 2012. It marked his fourth (third directorial) collaboration with Jean-Claude Van Damme.

### _O.J.: Made in America_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Hyams&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: O.J.: Made in America")]

Hyams was interviewed by [Ezra Edelman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezra_Edelman "Ezra Edelman") in the latter's documentary _[O.J.: Made in America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O.J.:\_Made\_in\_America "O.J.: Made in America")_, which touched on Hyams' former friendship with [O. J. Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O._J._Simpson "O. J. Simpson"), whom he had directed in _Capricorn One_. In his interview, Hyams revealed his initial belief that Simpson was innocent of [murdering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O._J._Simpson_murder_case "O. J. Simpson murder case") his ex-wife [Nicole Brown Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Brown_Simpson "Nicole Brown Simpson") and her friend [Ron Goldman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Goldman "Ron Goldman"), but began to have doubts following the revelation of DNA evidence that suggested otherwise. Hyams said he felt particularly betrayed when Simpson continued to insist that he was innocent when Hyams' friend also began to voice his doubts about Simpson's innocence. Following Simpson's acquittal, Hyams stated that he found the African-American celebration of the acquittal to be particularly offensive and hurtful, and later severed his ties with Simpson.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Hyams&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Personal life")]

On December 19, 1964, Hyams married George-Ann Spota, with whom he has three sons. His first son, Chris Hyams, was the CEO of the job search website [Indeed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indeed "Indeed"). His second son, [John Hyams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hyams "John Hyams"), is also a film director; Peter performed cinematography duties on John's film _[Universal Soldier: Regeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal\_Soldier:\_Regeneration "Universal Soldier: Regeneration")_. His third son, Nick Hyams, works as a [battle rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_rap "Battle rap") promoter and host under the name Lush One.

## Trademark

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Hyams&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Trademark")]

Hyams is known for being his own [cinematographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematographer "Cinematographer") on the movies he has directed since 1984.

As a reference to his wife's family, there is a minor character named Spota in many of his films, including those which he only wrote (such as 1980's _[The Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hunter\_(1980\_film) "The Hunter (1980 film)")_); the exceptions being _A Sound of Thunder_ (although there was a market called "Spota's"), _End of Days_ (although there was a bar called "Spota's"), _Narrow Margin_, _Running Scared_, _2010_, _Hanover Street_ and _Peeper_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hyams#cite_note-platniumcelebs-14) In _Hanover Street_, Harrison Ford pilots a B-25 bomber named Gorgeous George-Ann.
